    Industry News: Researchers Find AI Is Accelerating Vulnerability Discovery

    📅 28 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (498 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thejournal

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • AI-powered vulnerability research is contributing to a major increase in security updates, raising concerns that IT teams could fall behind as patching demands grow, according to cybersecurity manufacturer ThreatDown.
    • In a recent blog post, the company stated that in September 2026, vendors addressed 998 common vulnerabilities and exposures (CVEs) around Patch Tuesday, compared with 96 during the same period last year.
    • The researchers point to advanced AI models, including Anthropic's Claude Mythos Preview, as a major factor behind the increase in vulnerability discovery.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    AI-powered vulnerability research is contributing to a major increase in security updates, raising concerns that IT teams could fall behind as patching demands grow, according to cybersecurity manufacturer ThreatDown.

    In a recent blog post, the company stated that in September 2026, vendors addressed 998 common vulnerabilities and exposures (CVEs) around Patch Tuesday, compared with 96 during the same period last year. In addition, the three-month rolling average of patched Linux kernel vulnerabilities tripled year over year, while Google's Chrome browser experienced a 36-fold increase.

    The researchers point to advanced AI models, including Anthropic's Claude Mythos Preview, as a major factor behind the increase in vulnerability discovery.

    Introduced in April 2026, Mythos Preview is being used through Project Glasswing, an initiative involving Microsoft, the Linux Foundation and other organizations to identify vulnerabilities in critical software.

    While AI could ultimately make software more secure, the cybersecurity firm warns that vulnerability discovery is accelerating faster than organizations can deploy fixes.

    IT teams must still evaluate patches, test compatibility and schedule updates without disrupting critical business operations.

    The challenge is particularly significant for organizations already struggling with patch management.

    The cybersecurity vendor cites Verizon's 2026 Data Breach Investigations Report, which found that 35% of known actively exploited vulnerabilities remained unpatched after 28 days in 2025.

    Ryan Powell, vice president of IT and security at ThreatDown, said automated patching systems can help organizations manage the growing workload. However, additional patches still require more testing and validation, increasing operational overhead and the risks associated with frequent system changes.

    The report also highlights the risks of vulnerabilities in widely used software components such as OpenSSL, embedded in applications, network devices, and security products.

    Unlike standalone applications, these components often depend on downstream vendors to release updates before organizations can deploy fixes.

    According to recent reports, the security firm's analysis points to CVE-2022-0778, an OpenSSL vulnerability patched in March 2022, as an example. Some affected products did not receive updates until several months later.

    As AI accelerates vulnerability discovery, these dependencies could delay remediation and extend organizations' exposure to known security flaws.

    ThreatDown's findings illustrate a growing challenge for enterprise cybersecurity: AI is making vulnerabilities easier to discover but fixing them remains a complex and time-consuming process.

    For the full report, visit the ThreatDown blog here.

    The heads of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Hugging Face recently joined AI researcher Yoshua Bengio at the United Nations headquarters in Upcoming York to warn the UN Security Council about the security risks of increasingly capable AI.

    While security teams have invested heavily in e-mail protection, endpoint security, and identity controls, newly introduced research from Fortra suggests one challenge remains difficult to solve: customers.

    Research released around the recent Black Hat USA 2026 conference demonstrates that artificial intelligence is increasing the speed and scale of cybersecurity activity without replacing the attack methods defenders already face.

    Enterprise AI projects are running into infrastructure questions as organizations move from planning toward deployment, according to recent research from Digital Realty.

    Tech Report: Before & After: This Couple Planned to Flip a 62-Year-Old Fixer-Upper, Then Made It Their Home Instead

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (965 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housebeautiful

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, designer Claire Thompson has a theory about renovating a house alongside your significant other: If your relationship can survive that, it can probably survive anything.
    • It has been revealed that built in 1964, the five-bedroom property hadn’t been meaningfully upgraded in decades.
    • The decision to stay rather than sell came with a change in approach.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, designer Claire Thompson has a theory about renovating a house alongside your significant other: If your relationship can survive that, it can probably survive anything. In 2021, she and her now-husband, Will, purchased a nearly 5,000-square-foot home in Jackson, Mississippi’s Eastover neighborhood, with prepares to renovate the property and flip it for a profit. By 2022, they were engaged in the unfinished kitchen. Four years later, they’re still there, now with a baby daughter and a house that looks very little like the one they originally intended to sell.

    It has been revealed that built in 1964, the five-bedroom property hadn’t been meaningfully upgraded in decades. The rooms were compartmentalized, the finishes were dated, and the quirky floor strategy presented a few head-scratching challenges, like a second-floor dining room entirely removed from the kitchen below. But Thompson, who introduced her design business in 2020, saw something worth holding onto. “I promptly fell in love with the bones of the home, the lot the home is positioned on, and of course the neighborhood and the street itself,” she recalls.

    The decision to stay rather than sell came with a change in approach. Rather than gutting the house and putting in finishes they knew would grab buyers in a post-COVID market, the couple worked within the home’s existing footprint, opening up walls to encourage better circulation while preserving the individuality of each room. The kitchen, once closed off at either end, now connects to a light-filled breakfast nook and an inviting keeping room, where damaged parquet floors and dated ceiling beams gave way to white oak underfoot and softly textured plaster overhead.

    Industry observers note that nearby, a former study became an inky, book-lined library, complete with an expanded bar. Even the upstairs dining room survived, despite its logistical inconveniences. “We decided to keep it because of the way it flows when we entertain and host showers or parties,” Thompson says. “I think a home that tells a story, like a nod to the past or an interesting quirk, only makes the home more intriguing.”.

    The renovation unfolded after hours, with Will building cabinetry and tackling electrical work late into the night. Some spaces were even renovated twice: first, with resale in mind, then with the more personal considerations of permanence. The home became a testing ground for Thompson’s design practice, but it also serves as something of a family scrapbook. “We grew together as individuals, as a couple, as business owners, and as creatives,” she indicates. “The home feels like us.”.

    FAST FACTSDesigner: Claire Thompson DesignLocation: Jackson, MississippiThe Space: A five-bedroom, four-and-a-half-bathroom home across 5,000 square feet.

    The kitchen layout didn’t change too much, but Thompson was able to completely upgrade its feel and functionality by opening up both ends—one to the breakfast nook, one to the keeping room—and adding a center island.

    “I really did not want upper cabinets in the kitchen, so we were very thoughtful in the functionality of the cabinetry,” she adds. “My husband loves to remind me that he built me 42 drawers for the kitchen. We have ample storage, while still making it aesthetically the way I envisioned.”.

    Industry observers note that now open to the kitchen, the breakfast nook acts as a natural overflow spot where the family eats most of their meals, casual dinners included. Removing the ceiling beams allowed Thompson to capture the feel of taller ceilings; while she wanted to keep the brick floors, opening up the walls meant she had to opt for new white oak for continuity.

    “We call this the keeping room since we opened it up to the kitchen,” explains Thompson. “This is the room we really live in day to day; it’s a laid-back and comfortable space.”.

    Recent findings suggest that the pair started by plastering just the fireplace, but then decided to extend the treatment throughout the rest of the room—it’s since become a signature finish for Thompson’s firm. “We now use this technique in almost every project,” she adds.

    Previously a study, the library was born of equal parts design instincts and necessity. “My husband has so many books that we decided to wrap the room with bookshelves,” explains Thompson, who also reworked a hallway to add a bar and powder bathroom. The whole space is drenched in a Roman clay finish (Black Star by Portola Paints), creating an enveloping retreat that has become a go-to for family movie nights.

    It has been revealed that also known as the family’s “Christmas tree room,” the formal living room is a soothing symphony of neutral hues and nubby textures. “The coffee table is one of my favorite purchases of all time,” Thompson adds. “I bought it to sell to a client but decided I couldn’t part with it! I also love to have my grandmother’s antique stool in here—it always makes me think of her and brings me joy.”.

    According to recent reports, perfectly balanced between sweet and sophisticated, 12-week-old daughter Margot’s bedroom was an opportunity for Thompson to lean into all things childhood magic. “She may never leave the bassinet in our primary bedroom, but she does have a cute room waiting for her if that ever happens!” she adds.

    Industry observers note that connected to the nursery through a Jack-and-Jill bathroom, this guest space could eventually become a bedroom for a second child. For now, though, it’s a comfortable spot for visiting guests, and a favorite hideout of Thompson’s “first baby,” pup Lemmon.

    Claire Thompson is the owner of Claire Thompson Design, a full-service firm specializing in designing, renovating, and furnishing beautiful, timeless homes. She works closely with clients to ensure their unique personalities and desires are perfectly captured by the design and that all their wishes and needs are met.

    The Biggest Spring 2027 Trends Celebrate Glamour and Individual Style

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1229 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, the breakout trends from the Spring 2027 highlights were all about personalization and styling, humanizing the process of getting dressed at a time when AI can generate nearly anything for you.
    • There was also a touch of glamour almost everywhere.
    • Sources indicate that and lest we forget, this was the season of the skirt—so much so that Miuccia Prada and Raf Simons sent 63 skirt looks down the Prada runway in Milan.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, the breakout trends from the Spring 2027 highlights were all about personalization and styling, humanizing the process of getting dressed at a time when AI can generate nearly anything for you. From the clashing of statement pieces at Chanel, Dries Van Noten, and Valentino to the coming-out party of the bra at Dior and Altuzarra, the spring runways celebrated self-expression.

    There was also a touch of glamour almost everywhere. Dressing for daytime took on a fresh sheen via the cummerbunds and opera pumps at Kallmeyer, the metallic gold at Saint Laurent, and the boas at Tory Burch. At Michael Rider’s Celine, utilitarian staples were reimagined in sophisticated silhouettes, while brands like C and Bode took classic straight-leg jeans and added embellishment in the form of sparkle and embroidery. This season was all about celebrating the joy of getting dressed, a principle we think should be applied year-round.

    Sources indicate that and lest we forget, this was the season of the skirt—so much so that Miuccia Prada and Raf Simons sent 63 skirt looks down the Prada runway in Milan. Some were embellished, some had sheer details, and almost all of them fell right below the knee.

    Now that fashion month has wrapped and we’ve had some time to digest what we saw on the runways, we’re rounding up our nine favorite trends from the spring 2027 collections. And because March is still months away, we’ve shopped out some ways to get a jump on the looks now.

    Recent findings suggest that mixed-and-matched looks were all over the runways. What felt upcoming here was the against-the-grain pattern play, which felt like a message about personal style—an exhortation from designers to stop worrying about following the rules and lean into whatever makes you feel good.

    Sources indicate that this approach allows you to play with things that are already in your wardrobe. Invest in a sparkly skirt to pair with a checkered shirt you already own, or pair a new jacquard jacket with some animal-print boots already in your rotation. The key to this trend is making it your own.

    Staud Samira Faux-Fur-Trimmed Jacket.

    Bode Asymmetrical Sequin-Embellished Fringed Skirt.

    Herbert Levine Two-Faced 80 Boot.

    Stripped-back had a whole latest meaning this season! Designers quite literally loosened up a few buttons, exposing delicate bras worn underneath shirting. (Granted, some looks like those at Prada and Tom Ford had just a bra as the top, but we’re going to save that one for warmer months.) What’s so appealing about this look is the contrast between the sexy underpinnings and the polished separates. There’s nothing like a little lace to spice things up, and we are here for it!

    Citizens of Humanity Wool Shirt.

    Gucci Pleated Silk Twill Midi Skirt.

    Borrowing from the boys isn’t new in fashion. Surely I’m not the only one who loves a Winchester banker shirt with monogrammed initials? But the tuxedo dressing trend—which started on the fall 2026 runways and will be going strong all spring—feels fresh. Designers placed a huge emphasis on the waist (I call it “waistmaxxing”), with the focal point of many looks being the cummerbund. A tuxedo jacket, tailored pants, and opera pumps would create a chic head-to-toe approach, but these pieces look just as cool individually. I love tuxedo pants dressed down with a white T-shirt, for example.

    Zw Collection Stripped Cummerbund Shirt.

    Toccin High-Waisted Tuxedo Trouser.

    We’ve seen neckerchiefs and bandanas trending in previous seasons, but in spring 2027, neckwear takes a decidedly glam turn with the rise of the feather boa. I loved how Tory Burch paired her boas with car coats and silky shirts with trousers, while Dior’s models wore them with extravagant blazers. Both made the case that these three-dimensional scarves should be worn during the day, which feels cool, unexpected, and very much in keeping with the season’s dressed-up turn.

    The Fresh Arrivals Ilkyaz Ozel Feather Scarf.

    According to recent reports, designers really did their duty this season for the uniform dressers out there. If you love a tonal neutral, there were plenty to choose from in updated silhouettes, from balloon-style cargo pants to work shirts with peplums. What made them feel extra special was the way they were accessorized—with bold, colorful heeled boots and a bright satin bag at Celine, or with neon sandal heels at Balenciaga.

    Co Camo Cotton-Blend Military Jacket.

    JW Anderson Parachute Drawstring Barrel-Leg Track Cargo Pants.

    In a recent development, the standout jeans this spring are covered in decadent sequins, embroidery, and beading. How fun is that? The key when it comes to styling is keeping your favorite basics on deck and building a look around the jeans. Whether you pair your statement denim with a classic white shirt for work (as seen at Dolce & Gabbana and Bode) or take them for a spin around the town with an equally dazzling top (like at Conner Ives), these are always a good idea—full stop.

    Stella McCartney Crystal Embellished Straight-Leg Jeans.

    Polo Ralph Lauren Embroidered Mid-Rise Straight-Leg Jeans.

    Hellessy Embellished Straight-Leg Jeans.

    Ramy Brook Lea Beaded High-Rise Wide-Leg Crop Jeans.

    Sources indicate that with the price of gold at an all-time high and the jewelry market turning to silver, it’s been a refreshing change of pace to see glowing golden hues on the runways. We saw some gold looks sprinkled throughout shows in Fresh York like Ralph Lauren and Fforme, but the collection that really took the medal was Anthony Vaccarello’s final Saint Laurent show, where almost every look had a golden element. From gold jacquard to silky liquid-looking gold tops, these separates can easily spruce up your favorite black trousers for the office or white jeans for a weekend lunch. Or, if you want to take home the trophy, try going head-to-toe gilded for an evening event.

    Dries Van Noten Jacquard Linen, Cotton, and Silk-Blend Coat.

    According to recent reports, it’s fair to say that it’s the year of the skirt. Prada may have leaned in hardest, but this classic bottom was all over the runways in every city. The key silhouette was a hybrid pencil/A-line hitting slightly below the knee. (And let me tell you, as a trouser girl, this still sits within my tailored wheelhouse.) There’s a wide range of skirts on the market and an equal range of freedom when it comes to the styling. Whether you pair your skirt with a sweater and loafers for the office or wear it with a sleeveless top and heels for a night out, it’s a piece that can take you just about anywhere.

    Massimo Dutti Pleated Bubble Hem Midi Skirt.

    Polo Ralph Lauren Belted Crinkled Shell-Trimmed Crepe Midi Skirt.

    Marni Black Crinkled Midi Skirt With Daisy Details.

    Simone Rocha Pleated Sheer Satin Midi Skirt.

    Coats aren’t necessarily what most people get excited about in spring—who wants to hide a cute outfit when it’s finally warm enough not to bundle up?—but spring 2027 will be an exception. The coats on the runway this season were much more directional, especially the ones we saw covered in embellishments and jingling and jangling down the catwalk. Next March and April, prepare to layer in pieces that feel equal parts charming and elegant.

    Dries Van Noten Embellished Wool Longline Coat.

    Chan Luu Midnight Studio Coat Black.

    Cinq à Sept Mariella Embellished Faux-Fur-Cuff Coat.

    Prabal Gurung Floral Jacquard Single-Breasted Car Coat.

    • Attackers are exploiting enterprises' own artificial intelligence systems and extending pressure beyond internal networks to employees and their families, according to a latest Semperis survey of organizations that suffered disruptive ransomware attacks.
    • According to recent reports, in a recent announcement, the manufacturer highlighted findings from its 2026 Ransomware Risk Report, which examines AI-related attack tactics, personal intimidation, and recovery preparedness.
    • Sources indicate that the sample has an key limit: This year's study included only organizations where at least one ransomware attack caused business disruption.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Attackers are exploiting enterprises' own artificial intelligence systems and extending pressure beyond internal networks to employees and their families, according to a latest Semperis survey of organizations that suffered disruptive ransomware attacks.

    According to recent reports, in a recent announcement, the manufacturer highlighted findings from its 2026 Ransomware Risk Report, which examines AI-related attack tactics, personal intimidation, and recovery preparedness. Censuswide surveyed 1,200 information technology and security professionals across nine countries and eight industry sectors in the first half of 2026.

    Sources indicate that the sample has an key limit: This year's study included only organizations where at least one ransomware attack caused business disruption. The results describe those victims' experiences, rather than the likelihood that an organization will suffer an attack. The report says that sampling approach changed from previous studies.

    Semperis sells identity security, recovery and crisis management products.

    In a recent development, the report says 84% of respondents experienced attacks that exploited AI in some way. Its breakdown distinguishes AI-based attacks, reported by 40%, from attacks that manipulated victims' own AI agents or systems, reported by 44%. That distinction matters: The broader figure covers both attackers using AI and attackers exploiting AI deployed inside an organization.

    Recent findings suggest that defensive use of AI also produced mixed responses. Nearly half of respondents, 49%, remarked they successfully used AI for detection or response, while 23% said their AI tools failed to detect or respond successfully. Those are survey responses about victimized organizations, rather than a controlled comparison of security products.

    Industry observers note that chris Inglis, former U.S. national cyber director and a Semperis strategic adviser, described the difficulty of recognizing AI's involvement. "Many attacks are not perceived as being aided and abetted by AI because they're just too slick, too sophisticated," he stated in the report.

    Data erasure, destruction, or release remained the most frequently reported threat, at 56%. Blackmail, extortion or public shaming followed at 41%, with system lockouts or operational sabotage at 40%. The report also recorded psychological intimidation at 23% and physical threats at 17%.

    The heads of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Hugging Face recently joined AI researcher Yoshua Bengio at the United Nations headquarters in Latest York to warn the UN Security Council about the security risks of increasingly capable AI.

    While security teams have invested heavily in e-mail protection, endpoint security, and identity controls, new research from Fortra suggests one challenge remains difficult to solve: users.

    Research released around the recent Black Hat USA 2026 conference demonstrates that artificial intelligence is increasing the speed and scale of cybersecurity activity without replacing the attack methods defenders already face.

    Enterprise AI projects are running into infrastructure questions as organizations move from planning toward deployment, according to recent research from Digital Realty.

    Dancing With the Stars just aired one of its best finales everrrrr, resulting in Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach being crowned winners! And apparently this was a best-case scenario for producers, who—per an insider—were hoping Ezra would win.

    “Producers are mildly panicking because in a best case scenario world, Ezra would win,” a source told The Sun ahead of the live finale on Tuesday night. “He is in producers’ mind the perfect representation of a winner for this season.”.

    Per the outlet, producers believe Ezra could be the show’s “golden boy,” but were worried that his live scores wouldn’t be high enough to net a win after noticing engagement on his social media had “dropped significantly.” But clearly fans came out in droves voting for Ezra and Daniella, which—combined with their perfect scores all night—resulted in them winning!

    In case you missed it, Ezra reflected on his beautiful freestyle routine in the skybox, and talked about his prosthetic unexpectedly coming off mid-performance. “It’s crazy.     The 15 Most Thoughtful Personalized Gifts

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1034 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It might only be November, but the holidays are just around the corner, and with Hanukkah starting early this year on December 4, I’m already collecting gifts for everyone I love.
    • In a recent development, the easiest way to make a gift special?
    • Think engraved ID bracelets and signet rings for the guys, birthstone bracelets and sparkly initial pendants for the women in your life, and personalized sports merch for the fan whose team is a whole personality trait.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It might only be November, but the holidays are just around the corner, and with Hanukkah starting early this year on December 4, I’m already collecting gifts for everyone I love. Getting ahead of the curve has its perks: fewer frantic shipping fees, for one, and enough time to find something that feels genuinely special.

    In a recent development, the easiest way to make a gift special? Get it personalized. Because who wants to tear through wrapping paper only to find the same thing everyone else is getting this season? Go the custom route, and even a classic gift feels like it was made just for them (because, well, it was).

    Think engraved ID bracelets and signet rings for the guys, birthstone bracelets and sparkly initial pendants for the women in your life, and personalized sports merch for the fan whose team is a whole personality trait. Add sentimental photo albums full of family memories and a few delightfully quirky surprises they’ll never see coming, and you’ve got a list worth getting a head start on. Here are some of our favorite personalized gift ideas for the holidays this year.

    Know someone who takes great pleasure in writing hand-written letters? Make their next correspondence even more exciting with personalized writing paper from Smythson. Customize everything from the size and color of the paper, the text and motif at the top of the paper, and the tissue lining and border on the envelopes.

    Engraved jewelry is one of the classiest personalized gifts you can get for someone, especially when it’s simple and refined like this ID chain bracelet from Miansai. I got this bracelet for my boyfriend with his name engraved on it for the holidays last year, and he wears it pretty much every day.

    A personalized jersey is a no-brainer for anyone with a favorite sports team. The Fanatics custom shop has merch for NFL, MLB, NBA, WNBA, NHL, MLS, and even college teams, so it really has something for every kind of sports fan. And it’s not just jerseys—there’s also custom drinkware, bags, accessories, and more.

    It has been revealed that even if your giftee isn’t super into astrology, they’ll appreciate a candle that’s just for them (or, well, anyone that shares their birthday). If they are into astrology, they’ll love all the fun facts about their birthday on the candle’s label, including their Zodiac sign, element, constellation, tarot card, and more. And all you have to know is their birthday, so it’s a pretty easy gift.

    It has been revealed that speaking of birthdays, birthstone jewelry is another classic gift that’s personalized by design. And all you have to know is their birth month to get it right. Brilliant Earth has a great selection of birthstone jewelry, from pendant necklaces and colorful earrings to gemstone tennis bracelets and rings. You can even add multiple birthstones to this eternity lab diamond ring, so you can personalize it with the birthstones of everyone in your family.

    For the one who spends their weekends on the golf course: They’ll truly impress their golf buddies with a box of personalized golf balls. And it comes with tees, a divot tool, and poker-chip ball markers so they have everything they need.

    Industry observers note that if you have the time and want to do something really special, order one of these luxury lighters from S.T. Dupont and get it engraved in person at a local engraving shop or jewelry repair store. The extra effort will show, and your giftee will have something to carry with them wherever they go for years to come.

    You’ll have fun playing around with all the features in Ralph Lauren’s online custom hat maker—we certainly have. Choose the color and add a name, logo, or monogram, and the result will be a one-of-a-kind baseball cap your giftee will wear all the time.

    Don’t just print out a photo and call it a day; get it printed on glass for something truly unique. Upload your photo to Fracture and personalize it even more with colorful borders, templates, frames, and stands.

    Ever gone into a comic book store and seen the walls of Funko POP action figures from every franchise you can imagine? Having cute action figures of all your favorite Star Wars characters is great, but imagine how cool it would be to give someone an action figure of themself. With Funko POP, you can do just that—and you’ll have fun building it. You can even get a pair of Funko POP figures, so you can include yourself in it, too.

    According to recent reports, if you’re looking for a romantic personalized gift for your partner, surprise them with a watercolor painting of the place where you had your first date or the spot where you got engaged. Whether it was a local coffee shop, beloved movie theater, or beautiful outdoor space, it’ll look good painted above your names.

    According to recent reports, in a world where everything is online and in the cloud, a physical photo album is all the more sentimental and special. Artifact Uprising makes putting together a photo album easy, and the result is high quality and beautiful. It’s something they’ll want to display on their coffee table for everyone to see.

    According to recent reports, gifts based on birthdays is a common theme in this gift guide, but what can we say? It’s an easy way to personalize stuff. If they’re a history buff (or just love reading the news), they’ll enjoy flipping through this customized book of newspaper headlines from their birthday through the years.

    You know that person who is absolutely obsessed with their dog or cat? (Okay, it’s me.) They’ll obsess over any gift that has to do with their beloved pet, like this custom sweatshirt embroidered with the face of their dog or cat. Just upload a photo of their pet (you can probably find one on their Facebook or Instagram) and choose a sweater color and size.

    Recent findings suggest that A customized L.L. Bean tote bag is something they’ll use all the time. It’s one of our favorite gifts of all time, and it’s an absolute classic.

    IDC Report Finds Significant Gap Between AI Spending and Measurable Financial Returns

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nearly 70% of organizations report a significant gap between artificial intelligence spending and measurable financial returns, according to a recent survey by IDC.
    • The research firm's 2026 Worldwide AI Economics and Cost of Ownership Survey found that 69% reported such a gap, while only 15% had achieved an AI return on investment exceeding 100%.
    • In a separate May 2026 survey, 73% of respondents identified excessive AI costs as a significant risk.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nearly 70% of organizations report a significant gap between artificial intelligence spending and measurable financial returns, according to a recent survey by IDC.

    The research firm's 2026 Worldwide AI Economics and Cost of Ownership Survey found that 69% reported such a gap, while only 15% had achieved an AI return on investment exceeding 100%.

    In a separate May 2026 survey, 73% of respondents identified excessive AI costs as a significant risk.

    IDC highlighted the findings in an October 20 analysis examining what enterprise customers expect from AI technology vendors.

    Enterprise customers are placing greater emphasis on measurable business outcomes when evaluating AI products, according to IDC.

    The firm identified three priorities for vendors: demonstrating financial value, addressing governance and security requirements, and building support beyond IT departments.

    Industry observers note that the analysis also highlighted the gap between initial agentic AI deployments and broader adoption. Although 80% of organizations have started deploying agentic AI, only 17% are using it across the enterprise.

    IDC stated evaluating AI investments can be difficult when the technology changes how employees work and how business processes operate.

    The firm expects AI infrastructure capacity to catch up with demand around 2029, potentially easing costs. Until then, vendors face pressure to demonstrate the long-term financial value of their products.

    It has been revealed that AI funding decisions involve a broad range of executives. IDC's September 2026 C-Suite Tech Survey found that CIOs and CTOs were involved in 63% of those decisions, business-function executives in 62%, and chief financial officers in 61%.

    A separate IDC survey found that 42% of CEOs planned to hire a chief AI officer within the next 12 months.

    Buyers also reported concerns about the products and terms vendors offer. Limited integration with existing systems, insufficient model and data transparency, and concerns about vendor lock-in were each cited by 34% of respondents.

    Overpromising and underdelivering, along with unclear pricing models, were each cited by 31%.

    IDC said vendors need to substantiate financial returns and address security and governance requirements while working with decision-makers across IT, finance, and other business departments.

    For more information, go to the IDC blog.

    Microsoft is combining its security information and event management and threat protection products within Microsoft Defender, creating what the manufacturer calls an Integrated Security Operations Center built for an era of AI-driven attacks.

    Enterprise AI spending is growing faster than the number of organizations paying for it, according to a newly introduced Menlo Ventures report that points to a shift from buying access for employees to financing work performed by agents.

    Recent findings suggest that at a fundamental level, screen time policies and laws aim to address academic achievement by balancing digital instruction with traditional teaching methods. But they do not tackle how devices are used.

    The artificial intelligence industry is expected to generate an extraordinary $2.67 trillion in worldwide spending this year, according to a fresh forecast from Gartner.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Amber Glenn and Pasha Pashkov came in second during an absolutely incredible Dancing With the Stars finale, and their flawless freestyle is even more impressive knowing how little sleep Amber’s running on. The Olympian told Variety that she was drug tested the night before the finale, saying, “I actually had...you saw the drug testing show up last night. Yeah, so didn’t get much sleep. Third time they’ve tested me this season, by the way, guys, what’s happening? So, I’m excited to get some rest.”.

    At this point you’re probably wondering if Dancing With the Stars is drug testing contestants, which, nope! As Variety notes in their Twitter caption, Amber is referring to being tested by USADA (United States Anti-Doping Agency), which is the “national anti-doping organization (NADO) in the United States for Olympic, Paralympic, Pan American, and Parapan American sport.”.

    As their website puts it, they’re “charged with managing the anti-doping program, including in-competition and out-of-competition testing, results management processes, drug reference resources, and athlete education for all United States Olympic & Paralympic Committee (USOPC) recognized sport national governing bodies, their athletes, and events.”.

    Sources indicate that since Amber is currently training for the U.S. Figure Skating Championships (taking place in Utah this January), she’s being tested by the USADA like all athletes. Which might come as a surprise to everyone who didn’t realize Amber’s been juggling training with DWTS!

    According to recent reports, her coach, Damon Allen, explained to KRDO “She's been balancing dance on a rigorous schedule with that, as well as, being able to continue training, getting ready for nationals in January. It's been tiring. But she knows how to recover, and she's got a regimen, and she knows how to take care of her body, and figure out how to be at the top of her game at all times, whether it's in the dance arena or back on the ice.”.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Say “Margaritaville,” and most of us will likely imagine a place with strong island vibes: beach chairs in the sand and colorful tropical drinks in hand. That ease and joy remain at the core of Margaritaville brand ethos, but a new collaboration with North Carolina’s venerable Hooker Furnishings reveals a more refined and nuanced side to Jimmy Buffett’s creative vision and style. Mixing warm palettes, natural materials, and layered textures, the furniture collection is at once down-to-earth and luxurious—gorgeous to the eye, yet made to be enjoyed and lived in.

    Recent findings suggest that another thing this collection makes clear about Buffett is that his love of the natural world went far beyond the beach. He had a home for nearly 50 years in Snowmass, Colorado, and the natural beauty of that part of the world was as much of a muse as his legendary island life.

    In a recent development, both come alive in four lifestyle concepts the designers envisioned as they created the collection: there’s Paradise Valley, in which warm leathers, sustainable wood, and earth-tone textures draw inspiration from the Rocky Mountain vistas of the Centennial State; St. Somewhere, with playful Caribbean beach-town elements and subtle nods to surf culture; Island Reserve, which pairs performance materials with elegantly-crafted teak-wood or wicker chairs and sofas to make outdoor entertaining feel as elevated as indoor; and the JWB Signature line, which, among other things, showcases some of the most elegantly designed recliners around, inspired by the “timeless cool” of the man himself.

    So while you won’t find an actual hammock or porch swing in this collection, you will discover well-crafted oak beds, plush sectionals, and outdoor furniture that evoke the same dreamy vision and ease Buffett’s songs and stories are known for. Here are five pieces to help you start creating your own slice of paradise.

    The intention behind this collection was to create furniture that encourages people to gather and enjoy time together. The Sandbar sectional does the trick, with power recline in the left chairs, lumbar support throughout, hidden Bluetooth speakers to create a surround-sound experience, pop-out cupholders in the center console for easy drink access (and to help avoid unwanted spills), and hidden storage for cozy blankets and throws. And when you need to make room for overnight guests, planned or otherwise, a pull-out full sleeper lives inside the armless loveseat.

    The handcrafted glass base and organic sea foam stone top have this accent table almost doing double-duty as a piece of sculpture. The modernist line and soft color palette would look just as at home in a house by the shore as it would as an accent piece in an eclectic, maximalist living room in the suburbs. At just 14 inches in diameter and 22 inches high, it’s also petite enough to make a statement in smaller spaces.

    Your bedroom should feel like a sanctuary, and this white-oak poster bed will certainly make it feel that way. The striking cross-beam canopy defines the space between the outside world and the intimate space within; so together with the airy, sunbleached wood and neutral palette, it’ll have you drifting off to sleep each night feeling like you’re at a five-star tropical resort.

    According to recent reports, you can’t exactly embody the Margaritaville lifestyle without someplace to mix up Buffett’s signature cocktail, along with other favorites. This bar cabinet has the sleek look of a midcentury console, but with a twist: the powder blue on the doors is a painted finish, layered over woven linen to give the exterior subtle texture and visual depth. The interior is made of white oak and has multiple shelving areas, hanging stemware storage, an adjustable stone shelf, and removable wine-storage partitions for plenty of glassware, bottles, cocktail shakers, and more. The coral-design handles are, of course, a nod to the brand’s island heritage.

    At first glance, this looks like a beautifully simple wood pub table, but once guests sit down for dinner or a cocktail, they’ll notice its more playful details. Made with warm maple veneers and contrasting walnut accents, the whimsical counter-height table is designed to look like a surfboard. It’s intended to draw you in and encourage you to relax and savor the moment, whether you’re settling in with your morning coffee or together with friends to toast to a beach sunset.

    Louisa Jacobson’s Stylist on 10 Things That Inspire Her Red Carpet Looks

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1399 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In fashion, anything from niche archival research to a favorite film to an outfit you saw on your morning commute can make for inspiration.
    • Sources indicate that method dressing has become the road most traveled for Hollywood A-listers and their stylists.
    • In a recent development, “One thing that we are always aware of is not being the character she plays on TV, because she is more than that,” Jacobson’s stylist Edward Bowleg III told Harper’s Bazaar over Zoom.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In fashion, anything from niche archival research to a favorite film to an outfit you saw on your morning commute can make for inspiration. In our latest series 10 Things, we ask industry professionals and tastemakers to divulge the (you guessed it) 10 things that had the most impact on their aesthetic choices.

    Sources indicate that method dressing has become the road most traveled for Hollywood A-listers and their stylists. We’ve seen Zendaya and Law Roach turn out goddess-like dresses in homage to the actress’s role of Athena in The Odyssey, while the cast of the Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping has been channeling their outlandish onscreen personas into equally over-the-top red carpet looks. But even though period pieces present a prime opportunity for imitation, The Gilded Age star Louisa Jacobson, who plays Marian Brook in the Julian Fellowes series, says she’d rather dress like herself.

    In a recent development, “One thing that we are always aware of is not being the character she plays on TV, because she is more than that,” Jacobson’s stylist Edward Bowleg III told Harper’s Bazaar over Zoom. “She is a fully fleshed-out human being. She is Louisa and she is not Marian. That is an important distinction.”.

    According to recent reports, bowleg started working with the actress in 2022 after a mutual friend introduced them right around the time that The Gilded Age was set to premiere. The editorial stylist, who has worked for countless publications and brands like Hermès, Valentino, and Marc Jacobs, recalls his first official project with Jacobson: the 2022 Vanity Fair Oscars party, to which she wore an ivory off-the-shoulder Khaite gown with a Jeffrey Levinson clutch.

    Sources indicate that much has changed in the four years since that evening. “When she cut her hair short, that was the moment where a lot shifted,” said Bowleg. “It was a new her.” With the fresh haircut came a slew of delightfully unexpected red carpet moments, spanning a handful of tailored suits (and a cummerbund!) from Haider Ackermann’s Tom Ford, Conner Ives, and Calvin Klein Collection to a Dilara Findikoglu minidress with an armored bodice made from safety pins, metal accents, and a tattered chiffon train.

    It has been revealed that jacobson’s fashion evolution paralleled her own self-actualization. “Exploring sexual identity and being more free with that led to having more fun with experimental fashion and being unapologetic about what she likes and who she is,” remarked Bowleg. And it demonstrates: She’s been on a winning style streak recently.

    Coming off Jacobson’s recent Gilded Age press tour, which saw looks from Haider Ackermann’s Tom Ford, Ashlyn, Commission, and Mel Usine, Bowleg sat down with Bazaar to decode 10 influences that shaped his fashion choices, from Saint Laurent’s le smoking to an Azzedine Alaïa collection that lives rent-free in his head.

    According to recent reports, “We love tailoring, we love a suit. I could have her in a suit every day of the week. She went to her first Tom Ford show in March. When she told me she was invited, I was like ‘Oh my god, that is so cool,’ because I am a big fan. The 1996 Gucci show is burned into my brain. That is when my interest in fashion really began, so for me in a weird way it was almost like a full circle moment.

    It has been revealed that “I think with creative director Haider Ackermann’s tailoring in particular, the cut is so exquisite. When we have fittings with them, the only thing we are adjusting is the length of the trousers. There is also a confidence that she has when she puts them on. It’s very commanding. Then you mix that in with all of the elements—there is always a really sexy shoe that goes along with it.”.

    Recent findings suggest that “An image that could have been on the moodboard would be Helmut Newton’s photos of Saint Laurent’s Le Smoking with the women on the street in Paris. There is one image with a naked woman wearing just heels, standing with another woman in Le Smoking. That is very much the kind of vibe we are going for: mixing something sexy and feminine with tailoring, which is inherently masculine.”.

    “She went to the Met Gala this year with Dilara [Findikoglu]. When I had the conversation with Dilara and her team, the idea of armor came up. She had been to the Met ahead of our conversation, and she sent me all of these pictures that she had taken in the Medieval section where they have the helmets and the chain mail and the body armor. Those were just things that she loved and that became a big inspiration for the look.”.

    “For Louisa’s first Met Gala in 2022 (the red carpet theme was ‘Gilded Glamour, White Tie’) there was a John Singer Sargent painting of a woman in a black dress. The image helped direct our choice of look”—a futuristic gown with a gold trompe l'œil skeleton molded in leather and hand-painted in gold leaf from the Schiaparelli Spring/Summer 2022 Haute Couture collection by Daniel Roseberry.

    “I love Azzedine Alaïa. Specifically the 1986 show—the one with all of the bandage dressing with the cut-outs on the sides and the infamous denim and leather zip that goes all across the body. I believe Grace Jones walked. Even with the McQueen that she just wore, in a way it’s that sort of vibe—the bomber jacket but with the little skirt. It’s that kind of energy: A strong, powerful woman.”.

    According to recent reports, “There has been quite a bit of leather. The McQueen that she just wore, the Khaite full leather suit that she wore to the Vanity Fair Oscars party. She put it on, and it was like ‘This is fab.’ We were wondering if it was right for Vanity Fair and whether she would be the only one in a suit. I told Louisa that Zendaya had worn a suit the year before and I also was kind of like, ‘Fuck it, you look hot, this is great.’ Then there were two more leather Louis Vuitton looks that she wore. One was to the Vanity Fair Oscars party in 2024. And then before that, she wore a Vuitton look to the SAG Awards and the whole bodice was sculpted in leather, as well.”.

    “Hedi Slimane is a substantial inspiration of mine. Again, it’s a lot of tailoring, it’s leather, it’s a great silhouette. It’s the aesthetic overall, but in particular, it was the fall/winter 2006 collection that he did. There were things that were skinny and then there were things that were a bit more loose in terms of the trousers. There was a softness to the hardness of it all. It was still very edgy and a bit rock ‘n’ roll, but there was a soft glamour to it. That is something that I like with Louisa, even when it comes to the jewelry.”.

    It has been revealed that “I am really curious to see what Pieter Mulier will do with Versace and Atelier Versace is in January. [I should also say that] I am obsessed with Donatella Versace. When I started looking at all things [high] fashion, Donatella was another designer that I loved. That glamour and excess and sexiness—she is unapologetically who she is.”.

    In a recent development, “With music and ‘90s hip-hop, you look at the bling, the diamonds, and things like that. I love a great jewelry moment, so accessorizing Louisa’s looks with the right jewelry is always crucial part to me. I love diamonds. When she recently went to a Tiffany & Co. event [in Ashlyn], we initially had our brooch up on the lapel where you would traditionally see it. Then she was like, ‘It doesn’t feel right.’ So I moved it down to the peplum of the jacket. It was a substantial, big yellow diamond, which I was obsessed with. I just loved how much it sparkled and shined.”.

    Recent findings suggest that “Helmut Lang is also a big inspiration. There is a Spring 1998 men's collection and a Spring 1999 collection that I think about a lot in terms of silhouette and things that still resonate today. It all comes from having researched some of those collections in the past, so they tend to be recurring elements in the work.”.

    Industry News: Report: Global Ransomware Attacks Rise 23% in Q3

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Global ransomware activity increased 23% in the third quarter of 2026, with organizations in North America and Europe accounting for the largest share of attacks, according to cybersecurity firm NCC Group.
    • The company's Cyber Threat Intelligence Report Review of Q3 2026 recorded 2,865 ransomware victim claims, up from 2,325 in the previous quarter.
    • According to recent reports, despite the quarterly increase, attacks declined 26% month over month in September to 821.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Global ransomware activity increased 23% in the third quarter of 2026, with organizations in North America and Europe accounting for the largest share of attacks, according to cybersecurity firm NCC Group.

    The company's Cyber Threat Intelligence Report Review of Q3 2026 recorded 2,865 ransomware victim claims, up from 2,325 in the previous quarter.

    According to recent reports, despite the quarterly increase, attacks declined 26% month over month in September to 821. North America recorded the most attacks that month with 390, followed by Europe with 211.

    It has been revealed that the industrial sector accounted for 29% of quarterly attacks, while Qilin remained the most active ransomware group for the sixth consecutive quarter, recording 365 victims. The Gentlemen followed with 356, and INC Ransom ranked third with 109.

    The report highlighted a July cyber attack against a small UK power generation facility that forced operations to stop for approximately four days.

    Although the incident did not affect the national electricity grid, it demonstrated how cyber attacks can disrupt physical infrastructure.

    The security researchers said the incident was consistent with techniques previously associated with Iranian-affiliated campaigns, including attacks against internet-exposed industrial controllers.

    However, the UK government has not formally attributed the attack, and the techniques used remain unconfirmed.

    The report also identified growing security challenges as organizations connect traditional IT networks with operational technology (OT) systems for remote maintenance and centralized management.

    The firm recommended network segmentation, stronger privileged-access controls, and continuous monitoring of OT environments.

    The research found that more than 40 vulnerabilities affecting enterprise applications, VPN appliances, e-mail gateways, and management platforms were added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog during the quarter.

    The report examined Gunra, a ransomware-as-a-service operation that has targeted 53 victims across multiple industries as of Q3.

    According to the cybersecurity manufacturer, Gunra exploited vulnerabilities CVE-2024-55591 and CVE-2025-24472 in internet-facing Fortinet devices to gain access to corporate networks.

    The group also used stolen credentials, session hijacking, and administrative tools to move between systems before deploying ransomware.

    Other emerging ransomware groups included Deadlock and Storm, with the latter claiming 78 victims by the end of September.

    Researchers also observed initial access brokers advertising compromised VPN, Remote Desktop Protocol, and SSH access, alongside access to cloud identities, source code repositories, and security management platforms.

    The quarterly review also highlighted BraZetsu, an AI-enhanced Windows malware framework that evolved into a specialized initial access toolkit.

    According to the report, BraZetsu uses AI models to automate victim profiling, analyze compromised environments, and identify valuable corporate systems.

    The framework searches for enterprise software, financial data, digital certificates, and cloud credentials, helping operators identify compromised access that can be sold to other cyber criminals.

    The cybersecurity firm also identified risks involving legitimate AI agents, including prompt injection, excessive permissions, and unintended access to external systems.

    It has been revealed that the report cited incidents involving U.S. and Australian government systems as examples of agents accessing resources beyond their intended scope.

    Researchers warned that these incidents do not necessarily involve malicious intent but can create consequences resembling conventional cyber intrusions.

    For the full report, visit the NCC Group site.

    Microsoft is combining its security information and event management and threat protection products within Microsoft Defender, creating what the company calls an Integrated Security Operations Center built for an era of AI-driven attacks.

    Enterprise AI spending is growing faster than the number of organizations paying for it, according to a fresh Menlo Ventures report that points to a shift from buying access for employees to financing work performed by agents.

    At a fundamental level, screen time policies and laws aim to address academic achievement by balancing digital instruction with traditional teaching methods. But they do not tackle how devices are used.

    The artificial intelligence industry is expected to generate an extraordinary $2.67 trillion in worldwide spending this year, according to a newly introduced forecast from Gartner.

But while some of William’s proposed changes seem logical, others have come as a surprise to royal insiders.

    Chatting to Radar Online about his newly introduced book, Tom Sykes remarked that friends of William revealed he intends to scrap his children’s titles in the name of “liberation.”.

    According to recent reports, according to the author of Dukes of Hazard: Harry, Andrew and Edward VIII: The Spares Who Shook the Throne, while Prince George will inherit the throne, William is keen for Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis to have other options.     “He’s gone and looked under the bonnet and is now making really difficult decisions and changing an organization that hasn’t been changed for a very long time,” another insider told Radar Online.

    Sources indicate that but if William’s plan goes ahead, it wouldn’t be the first time that members of the royal family went without their HRH titles. Both Princess Anne and Prince Edward opted out of giving their children royal titles, and the former Prince Andrew was shockingly stripped of his just last year.

    Previously speaking about the decision to not bestow her children with a fancy title, Prince Edward’s wife, Sophie Wessex, told The Sunday Times, “We try to bring them up with the understanding they are very likely to have to work for a living.”.

    The Duchess of Edinburgh went on, “Hence, we made the decision not to use HRH titles.”.

    From the stands, F1 regulars like Keanu Reeves and Kim Kardashian took it all in, with the latter there to cheer on her boyfriend, Lewis Hamilton (who finished 7th for Ferrari). Meanwhile, other A-listers in attendance included Lisa, Teyana Taylor, Venus Williams, Sarah Michelle Gellar, Nina Dobrev, Rachel Brosnahan, and Eiza González, who moved between qualifiers, races, parties, and more.

    Sources indicate that el Niño be damned. Winter is just around the corner, and even in a very weird year for weather, I can guarantee you this: There are cold days ahead. It pays to be prepared for them. And you could do a whole lot worse, preparation-wise, than the upcoming collaboration between Buck Mason and Sierra Designs.

    Sources indicate that you probably know both brands already, but just in case you don’t, here’s a brief primer. Buck Mason, founded in 2013, makes the kind of cool-but-accessible menswear staples that you can build an entire wardrobe around. Sierra Designs is one of the OG American outdoors brands, founded in 1965 and responsible for iconic designs like the 60/40 mountain parka and all sorts of other equipment and clothing built for exploring nature. Both, handily enough, were born in California—and today they released their first-ever collaboration.

    It has been revealed that the new collection draws heavily from Sierra Designs’ ‘70s heyday, with reworked versions of an archival down jacket and vest serving as the stars of the show. Both are made from lightweight Japanese nylon and utilize a 600-fill-power, 80/20 blend of down and feathers for insulation. They’re complemented by a range of vintage-y tees, thermals, totes, and caps.

    Industry observers note that the overall vibe is easygoing and not too techy—exactly the sort of stuff you’ll want to wear in everyday life, not just on some windswept summit. Which is what makes it so damn good. There’s no shortage of high-performance winter gear out there, but much of it falls short on the style front. This is the sort of stuff that’ll do the job but won’t have you looking like you just finished a black-diamond run. Wear it with chinos and hiking boots or jeans and sneakers. To the coffee shop on a blustery morning or the park for a day out with the family. Or, yeah, even in the great outdoors. Just make sure to snag whatever you like soon, as Buck Mason’s collaborations have a nasty habit of selling out.

    Microsoft is introducing upcoming tools within its sovereign cloud offerings designed to give organizations tighter control over where their data resides, who can access it, and how critical systems operate, especially in light of AI becoming a bigger part of enterprise infrastructure.

    Recent findings suggest that in a recent announcement, Douglas Phillips, president and chief technology officer of Microsoft Specialized Clouds, outlined updates spanning public cloud, private cloud, and partner environments. The changes target governments, regulated industries, and organizations that need tighter control over sensitive workloads without abandoning cloud-based AI capabilities.

    "Digital sovereignty should give organizations greater control and security over the technology they depend on, while continuing to innovate," Phillips wrote.

    One of the biggest additions is Microsoft's Sovereign Control Panel, which will enter public preview at Microsoft Ignite. Available through the Azure portal, the tool will give IT administrators one place to manage data sovereignty settings, spot compliance concerns, and identify potential risks that could disrupt operations.

    Microsoft is also tightening controls over who can access sensitive systems. Its Data Guardian feature will require oversight by personnel based in Europe when Microsoft engineers access certain production systems in the European Union and European Free Trade Association. Another tool, Production Touch Ledger, will keep tamper-resistant records of that access, giving organizations a clearer picture of who accessed their systems and what they did.

    It has been revealed that microsoft is also giving customers more control over encryption. External key management with Azure Managed HSM is now generally available, letting organizations keep their main encryption keys on hardware they own or manage outside Microsoft's cloud.

    The tech giant is also expanding its Sovereign Private Cloud offerings, giving organizations more options to run systems with or without an internet connection. New capabilities include GitHub Enterprise Local, GitHub Copilot with locally hosted AI models, and additional data services running on Azure Local.

    The push for greater operational control comes as Microsoft is also reconsidering how enterprises should secure increasingly autonomous AI systems.

    As reported by Redmond magazine, Microsoft is expanding Project Perception to address risks posed by what the company calls "agentic insiders," AI agents capable of accessing sensitive information and performing actions without constant human supervision.

    That initiative introduces plans for Guardian Agents, specialized security agents designed to monitor other AI systems, evaluate their behavior and intervene when their actions become risky.

    "Monitoring and securing those agents must become continuous," mentioned Hayete Gallot, executive vice president of Microsoft Security.

    Sources indicate that project Perception is about limiting what AI agents can do. Microsoft's sovereign cloud expansion tackles a different set of questions: where those systems run, who gets to administer them, and how the data stays protected.

    Taken together, the two efforts point to a shift in Microsoft's enterprise AI strategy. The company is putting more weight on oversight, not just automation.

    Phillips noted AI is making these questions more pressing as organizations roll out intelligent systems across sensitive business processes and critical infrastructure.

    For more information, go to the Microsoft blog.

    Chris Paoli (@ChrisPaoli5) is the associate editor for Converge360.

    The heads of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Hugging Face recently joined AI researcher Yoshua Bengio at the United Nations headquarters in Fresh York to warn the UN Security Council about the security risks of increasingly capable AI.

    While security teams have invested heavily in e-mail protection, endpoint security, and identity controls, upcoming research from Fortra suggests one challenge remains difficult to solve: owners.

    Research released around the recent Black Hat USA 2026 conference demonstrates that artificial intelligence is increasing the speed and scale of cybersecurity activity without replacing the attack methods defenders already face.

    Enterprise AI projects are running into infrastructure questions as organizations move from planning toward deployment, according to recent research from Digital Realty.

    Tech Report: How to Do a Chrome Manicure Over Regular Nail Polish If You’re Feeling Really Brave

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1515 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish

    • There are, in my view, four types of DIY nail art: Manicures that are as easy to do as they look, designs looks complicated but are actually pretty simple, motifs that are exactly as hard as they look, and nail art that seems like it should be a breeze but are actually a pain in the butt.
    • Recent findings suggest that in fact, chrome powder paired with regular polish is so finicky that some experts feel like it’s not worth the hassle to even try.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that we may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love. Promise.

    There are, in my view, four types of DIY nail art: Manicures that are as easy to do as they look, designs looks complicated but are actually pretty simple, motifs that are exactly as hard as they look, and nail art that seems like it should be a breeze but are actually a pain in the butt. Chrome manicures fall into that last category, especially if you’re trying to layer the metallic powder over regular polish.

    Recent findings suggest that in fact, chrome powder paired with regular polish is so finicky that some experts feel like it’s not worth the hassle to even try. “In my experience, improvising with loose chrome pigment over regular polish can become a long, tedious process with inconsistent results,” notes nail artist Max Estrada. “A manicure should be a little luxury, not an endurance examination.”.

    It’s a fair warning: Chrome definitely works best with gel, and it’s going to take a lot of trial and error to get that mirror-like shine on top of regular polish. But there are lots of legit reasons that some people avoid gel in their at-home manicure station (allergies... you have to buy a whole UV setup... it’s tedious to remove...), and those people might still want to try the chocolate chrome look so beloved by Hailey Bieber right now. (Also, some of us are just artistic masochists who find it reasonable that the cost of creative satisfaction would be some failed attempts and frustrated tears.).

    In a recent development, so, if you’re feeling up for the challenge—and have a lot of time to wait for your polish to dry completely—here are some tips for getting a chrome manicure with regular polish. (Results absolutely not guaranteed!).

    According to recent reports, while you can use any regular polish you’d like as your base color for this, there are a few different techniques that can work for a chrome finish, says Jackie of @jackie.shades. However, she’s gotten so good at applying chrome over regular polish people on the internet are calling her approach “The Jackie Method,” so I’m going to stick with that. For that method, you’ll need:.

    It has been revealed that chrome is not very forgiving of lumps and bumps, so you’ll need to do some careful nail prep before you get started. In addition to the usual filing, hangnail trimming, and cuticle pushing, Jackie recommends a smoothing base coat like Halo Taco Smoothing Base or What’s Up Nails Hideaway Ridge to give you a smooth base to start on.

    As far as your station goes, Jackie emphasizes that chrome is messy. “Make sure you turn off any fans, work on a silicone mat or paper towel, try not to flick any dust into the air, and wear a face mask,” she says. That last point is because chrome powder is a super fine dust—you don’t want to breathe that in.

    Recent findings suggest that this is the method Jackie has found works best for her nails (and others on Instagram who’ve tried it say it works great for them too) but she leads with a massive disclaimer that everyone is different. “Some products work for some and not for others,” Jackie says. “If something doesn’t work out, just keep experimenting.”.

    According to recent reports, after your nails are prepped, apply thin layers of your color polish of choice. Keeping them thin is important, Jackie says, since this prevents air bubbles that will be noticeable once you add the chrome powder. Also, thin layers dry more rapidly.

    In a recent development, having completely dry polish is one of the biggest keys to success for this look. “The base polish should be dry enough that if you press on your nail plate with your finger, it doesn’t leave any dents,” Jackie states. In my experience, this can take hours with some polish (I told you this wasn’t some easy breezy DIY mani). If you want to be really safe, you could even paint the base color on the night and finish the next steps the following day.

    According to recent reports, next, you’ll be creating the tacky base for the chrome to stick to. While you can use any quick dry top coat here, Jackie recommends a 3-free (meaning it’s free of toluene, formaldehyde, and dibutyl phthalate) formula for ease. “ Toluene can sometimes cause certain nail polish colors to ‘bleed’ or ‘run’ so this just helps to avoid any unnecessary cleanup,” she notes.

    Again, you’ll need to let this layer dry until you don’t get any dents if you press into it. Luckily, this usually takes less than five minutes with a quick dry. “I cannot emphasize enough the importance of letting each layer dry,” Jackie says. “Most problems that come up (polish wrinkling, bubbles, weird texture, chrome looking cloudy etc.) are because one of the layers wasn't fully dry.”.

    Finally, the fun part. Jackie uses her finger to apply the chrome (but only on regular polish—doing so on gel could lead to skin irritation) but you can also use an eyeshadow sponge or cosmetic wedge.

    Sources indicate that to apply, tap your tool of choice into the chrome powder pot and gently wipe it onto the nail. Then, use the tool to buff the chrome into your nail until it creates a smooth, metallic finish. Once you’re happy with how it looks, use a big fluffy brush to brush away the excess.

    Once the chrome is applied, wait at least another 15 minutes to ensure the top coat underneath it is truly, 100% dry. Then, Jackie says to swipe a 240 grit buffer block along the free edge of your nail to remove any excess chrome powder. “Now, brush off any additional excess and use a clean cosmetic wedge to gently wipe and tap over the nail to get any leftover loose chrome,” she says.

    Recent findings suggest that after lots of trial and error, Jackie found that the alcohol-based top coat DRK Seal Glaze “keeps the mirror shine and stays on nails longer than a water-based top coat.” You’ll want to apply two coats of it at this point, waiting about 10 minutes (or until the cloudiness turns clear) in between each coat. Make sure you’re applying thin coats that go all the way to the edges of your nails—if you miss any spots, those areas could turn glittery. Then, wait at least 30 minutes for the glaze to dry completely.

    After everything is completely dry, you’ll want to finish with the same top coat you applied before the chrome powder. Even on gel polish chrome is notoriously prone to chipping, but Jackie claims this glaze + top coat combo helps with longevity, especially if you use the top coat to wrap the tip of your nail.

    Unlike with gels, removal is way easier than applying here: Jackie states you can take this off just like you would any other regular polish manicure.

    Industry observers note that if all of this is making your head spin, Estrada notes that there are some chrome-effect regular polishes that can get pretty close to this mirror-like finish. “A chrome-effect lacquer is an alternative finish, not a promise that every bottle will reproduce the same mirror effect as a professional pigment-and-gel system,” he says. “The important thing is to choose the right product for the finish you want, rather than expect an improvised combination to perform identically.” Sally Hansen and Essie, both sell chrome-effect polishes, though they do look more glittery than a true chrome finish. There’s no shame in this game, Estrada says: “There’s nothing wrong with taking the more straightforward route.”.

    I'm a Mom of Two, and This Ernesta Rug Gives Me That Luxe Look With the Easy Cleanup of a Washable Option
