    #215332. Breaking: Tom Hardy's 5 Most Stylish Characters, Ranked

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (755 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Esquire ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Tom Hardy's 5 Most Stylish Characters, Ranked

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (755 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Tom Hardy doesn’t usually play the good guy.
    • That’s partly down to the costume designers, who’ve given Hardy everything from ’60s East End tailoring to Steve McQueen-inspired ’70s outerwear, but it’s also down to Hardy, who has a particular knack for making a wardrobe feel like his own.
    • It has been revealed that so, we’ve dug through the archives to rank his best-dressed roles of all time, and one of them’s actually on TV right now.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tom Hardy doesn’t usually play the good guy. He’s been a forger, a fixer, a getaway driver, a rogue spy, and, in one of his more ambitious films, both halves of the most notorious twins in British crime (not that there’s much competition). Most of them are walking red flags, sure, but they’re red flags in great clothes.

    That’s partly down to the costume designers, who’ve given Hardy everything from ’60s East End tailoring to Steve McQueen-inspired ’70s outerwear, but it’s also down to Hardy, who has a particular knack for making a wardrobe feel like his own. Put him in a Western shirt or three-piece and he’ll look equally at home in both (and you’ll want to steal the look, either way).

    It has been revealed that so, we’ve dug through the archives to rank his best-dressed roles of all time, and one of them’s actually on TV right now. Consider it your new watch list—just ignore the red flags.

    Everyone remembers the spinning top and Joseph Gordon-Levitt’s three-piece, but the best-dressed man in Inception is the one who usually gets overlooked: Tom Hardy’s Eames. Costume designer Jeffrey Kurland imagined him as an expat from a Graham Greene novel, and every piece was made from scratch (even though half of it looks straight off a Dries Van Noten runway). Think batik-print shirts, collars spread over relaxed blazers, sharp trousers, and a wallet chain—basically clothes for a guy who spends too long sitting in the sun and definitely doesn’t wear SPF. Then there’s the watch: a gold tank-style antique Kurland picked up from the prop master’s collection—and he’s since forgotten the brand. Reddit’s watch sleuths are still on the case, 16 years and counting.

    In a recent development, legend gave its costume department a very crucial task: how do you tell Tom Hardy apart from Tom Hardy? Lead designer Caroline Harris and Soho tailor Chris Kerr solved it with buttons: Reggie, the charmer, wears single-breasted suits that feel safe and easy to trust. Ronnie, meanwhile, is the volatile one who gets three-piece double-breasted silhouettes with extra padding to make him look macho. On both sides, though, everything’s cut from vintage fabrics for a lived-in look straight from the hanger. Sixty years on, you could walk into any hotel bar dressed as either and nobody would bat an eye. Until you start talking business, that is.

    In a recent development, inspired by the real-world Cold War scandals that rocked British Intelligence, Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy follows the hunt for a Russian mole inside MI6 in 1973. So, as you might expect, it’s lots of men doing stuff in gray suits. Not Hardy’s Ricki Tarr, though. He’s the only agent with any personality, wardrobe-wise, all thanks to costume designer Jacqueline Durran. Her thinking? Steve McQueen on a mission: a shearling coat in Istanbul, a Baracuta Harrington in Paris, and not a standard suit in sight. The kind of menswear every guy on your FYP is wearing today—Hardy was just 15 years early.

    In MobLand, Pierce Brosnan and Helen Mirren head up the Harrigans, an Irish crime family at war on several fronts—and no one knows it better than Hardy. He plays Harry Da Souza, the guy they call when things go wrong, which seems to happen fairly often. Costume designer Rebecca Hale gave him a wardrobe for the job: a battered wax jacket when he’s taking care of the Cotswolds estate, say, or a significant overcoat when he’s doing business in the city. There’s one exception to the low-key menswear staples, though: his watch. In season one, he wore a solid gold Rolex GMT-Master II, which is reportedly the most valuable watch in the show. Pretty good for the hired help.

    In a recent development, mobLand isn’t Hardy’s first Guy Ritchie gangster part. In RocknRolla, he’s Handsome Bob, the Wild Bunch’s getaway driver. And while everyone else looks like they’d had someone ‘”taken care of” before lunch, Hardy’s low-key menswear staples make him look more like the boy next door. A faded denim shirt. A classic bomber with jeans. A blue checked Western shirt, open just far enough. All simple pieces that let his charm do its thing, which it does when he sweet-talks a lawyer into revealing who’s been grassing to the police. Four years earlier, he played Clarkie in Layer Cake, another member of a London crime crew but one with a very different wardrobe: slicked hair, blazers, open shirts, brandy, and cigars. Similar JD, just with a very different wardrobe.

    #215331. 9 Interior Trends Designers Are Officially Ditching in 2027

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1501 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Housebeautiful ↗ Open Full Page

    9 Interior Trends Designers Are Officially Ditching in 2027

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1501 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housebeautiful

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The end of the year is a great time to look back and reflect.
    • Recent findings suggest that we love predicting what’s going to be hot in home design for the upcoming seasons; however, you can’t talk about what’s going to be “in” without also touching on what’s going to be “out.” We asked a handful of designers to share what design choices and interior trends they saw a lot of in 2026 that they’re more than happy to leave behind in 2027.
    • We spend so much time making our interiors warm and reflective of our personalities, it would be a shame to ruin the look of these spaces by opting for one-dimensional lighting.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The end of the year is a great time to look back and reflect. When it comes to home design, there’s a lot to cover, from latest trends to furniture collaboration drops to specific internet-breaking interiors. One of our favorite things to do around this time is figure out what’s coming next in terms of interiors.

    Recent findings suggest that we love predicting what’s going to be hot in home design for the upcoming seasons; however, you can’t talk about what’s going to be “in” without also touching on what’s going to be “out.” We asked a handful of designers to share what design choices and interior trends they saw a lot of in 2026 that they’re more than happy to leave behind in 2027. Keep reading to find out the nine things they stated.

    We spend so much time making our interiors warm and reflective of our personalities, it would be a shame to ruin the look of these spaces by opting for one-dimensional lighting.

    Industry observers note that “It's time to move beyond relying on a single overhead fixture or wall-to-wall recessed lighting to illuminate an entire room,” designer Kristen Mendoza of Four Brothers Design + Build claims. “Flat, overly bright lighting can make even the most beautifully designed spaces feel sterile and uninviting.”.

    Instead, incorporating layers of lighting to add dimension and create a warm atmosphere is much better for your home. Sconces, picture lights, table lamps, and thoughtfully placed accent lighting at various heights throughout the room, Mendoza adds, give a space a more intimate touch.

    Sources indicate that “I also recommend using warm 2700K light sources on dimmers to flatter people, highlight architectural details, and bring out the natural beauty of materials,” she explains. “Lighting should be considered early in the design and construction process, not treated as an afterthought.”.

    According to recent reports, part of the appeal of “grandma chic” decor is that it’s been collected over time. The pieces show their age, the interior is imperfect, and it’s very clearly reflective of the homeowner’s personality and life. However, “there is a difference between a room that feels ‘collected over time’ and one that feels inherited all at once,” designer Stephanie Kraus explains, and she’s tired of seeing this false presentation on display in people’s homes.

    Industry observers note that “Heavy Roman shades with lots of fabric, chintz on top of chintz on top of chintz, fringe on every edge, etc.,” she adds. “One of these details in a room can be charming, but if you use them all together, the room can start to feel like a period movie set.”.

    It’s often clear when this eccentric aesthetic is manufactured rather than effortless. Instead of trying to make the “ideal” interior in the span of a month, be patient and work on your home over a greater span of time. That way, the end product will look authentic.

    Though curved sofas are massively popular right now and look gorgeous in a photograph, Kraus is ready to leave them in 2026. “A curved sofa rarely seats more than two people comfortably,” she says. “Once guests settle in, everyone ends up sitting awkwardly, and conversation feels harder than it should.”.

    She’s all for a sofa or couch being something that invites people in to linger over conversations and stay late into the night, and a kidney-shaped seat isn’t going to do that.

    Sources indicate that while designer Maggie Vollrath of Provision Studios loved seeing the return of decorative, playful details like ruffles and scalloped edges, she thinks we’ve gone a bit overboard in 2026. These touches are being applied to just about everything: upholstery, pillows, lampshades, bedding, furniture—the list could go on.

    “These details can be incredibly charming, but when they're repeated throughout an entire room, they begin to lose the very character that makes them special,” she says.

    Rather than treat every piece of a room with one of these details, Vollrath suggests opting for a scalloped lampshade or a beautifully tailored ruffled pillow instead to still capture that charm without drowning the space in them.

    In a recent development, “Limiting these details to one or two thoughtful applications allows them to feel intentional rather than overly thematic,” she adds. “Sometimes, the most interesting interiors are as much about what you choose to leave out as what you include.”.

    According to recent reports, “I'd love to see us move away from selecting materials simply because they imitate the appearance of something more expensive,” Vollrath explains. This goes beyond marble-printed contact paper and burl wood veneer; the designer means on a larger scale, like mass-produced tile that’s made to replicate the imperfections of handmade zellige.

    Recent findings suggest that “Part of what makes authentic zellige so beautiful is the craftsmanship and natural variation that comes from its production,” she notes. “When those qualities are artificially reproduced, I think we sometimes lose the very thing that made the original material special.”.

    She would rather see a greater appreciation for beautiful, honest materials at every price point, and if the exact thing a homeowner wants is out of budget, then her solution would be to pivot the idea altogether rather than find something cheaply made that looks like what they desire.

    “A classic Carrara marble paired with beautifully considered cabinetry can create an incredibly sophisticated interior, even when something as dramatic as Calacatta Viola isn't within the budget,” Vollrath explains.

    It has been revealed that we could probably say this every year, but it bears repeating: Don’t solely follow trends! “Just because something is trending doesn't mean it's right for your home,” designer Drew Michael Scott of Lone Fox claims. “Polka dots are having a moment right now, but they don't make sense in many homes, or dare I say, most homes.”.

    He suggests thinking of home trends as prompts that should get you to brainstorm new ideas for your space that actually fit your style. Take polka dots again. If you want to introduce a new pattern to your home, but you don’t particularly mesh with polka dots, try a stripe instead.

    Industry observers note that “If you try to force something you don't love into your home just because it's trending, you're going to drive yourself crazy,” he adds. Let’s leave this line of thinking back in 2026 once and for all.

    According to recent reports, while we love a good built-in bookshelf and wooden ceiling beam, those types of architectural details don’t always make sense in every single home. In 2026, as personality-filled interiors became more popular for everyone, a lot of homeowners looked into adding this type of millwork to their spaces as a way to add more visual interest and texture.

    “Decorative beams, arches, and elaborate millwork can feel forced when they don't make sense with the architecture of the home,” designer Dani Flax of Pearson Design Group argues. “I think there's a tendency to add these elements to make a space feel more interesting, but the result can actually take away from the architecture itself.”.

    A home in a modern farmhouse style, for example, would look a bit odd with an intricate ceiling medallion and excessive picture frame molding. Design your interior around the existing architecture and the style of your home, don’t incorporate these elements simply because they’re everywhere right now.

    The next year is not about playing it safe with your interiors—designers are tired of the stark white home. While ubiquitous gray and white color schemes had their time, they can often make a home feel generic and devoid of character.

    “In their place, we're embracing more intentional, tonal palettes and color drenching,” Mendoza says.

    You can still have a mostly white house, of course, but take a little risk and mix in some pops of color and pattern here and there, or choose a beautiful neutral wood tone for your cabinetry instead of a bright white paint.

    “Taking a considered color, whether it's a deep green, warm clay, or earthy mushroom, and carrying it across walls, trim, and cabinetry creates a cohesive, enveloping effect,” Mendoza adds. “The goal isn't necessarily to introduce more color, but to use it with greater confidence and purpose.”.

    This is definitely a hot take, but designer John Maloney McNamara of Coosa Interiors is ready to leave velvet upholstery behind. “I’ve tried, but velvet almost always reads as either a 1990s prom limo or a hotel lobby trying very hard,” he explains. “The sheen reveals every crush and bruise, and it ages into something that looks tired rather than loved.”.

    In a recent development, if you love the look of velvet, he suggests going with a mohair fabric instead, saying it has all of velvet’s depth and none of its shine. It also only gets better with age. And though he knows creamy bouclé has been overdone, Maloney McNamara thinks it deserves a reprise, but only in a rich color that can replace velvet still.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, let’s face it—all too often, travel is not so glamorous. With flight cancellations, long TSA lines, and schlepping luggage, you may not feel chic throughout it all, but your travel look can still be. Peak holiday season is here, and some of the busiest travel days are still ahead; we drew inspiration from a few of our favorite celebrities to bring you the best travel outfits for women, making your next excursion all the more stylish.

    According to recent reports, comfort is often top of mind, but that doesn’t mean you have to settle for just leggings. Katie Holmes highlighted how to wear a simple white button-down shirt and baggy patchwork jeans on a flight, adding comfortable soft loafers and a stylish houndstooth jacket—a cool spin on a relaxed travel outfit that still feels put together. Kendall Jenner went for something polished, wearing a silky cream matching set, while Naomi Watts sported a leather bomber jacket, T-shirt, wide-leg sweatpants, and bright-red sneakers, showing the many different directions you can take to fit your own personal style.

    Ahead, shop the 9 best travel outfits for women that will ensure your journey is just as good as the looks you packed.

    As Katie Holmes proves, you don’t always have to rely on leggings for the airport; instead, elevate your look with a white button-down shirt and baggy patchwork jeans. Styling those with a houndstooth jacket, gray cashmere knit, and soft leather loafers, you’ll look incredibly polished throughout your travel journey.

    Dunst Harrington Quilted Wool Jacket.

    Buck Mason Mainstay Cotton Shirt.

A sleeveless top and wide-leg pants instantly look stylish in the luxe fabric. Add classic accessories like a suede duffel bag, the Row’s leather flats, and a watch as small but impactful touches. For a little extra warmth, throw on your favorite wrap, cardigan, or coat.

    Breda Virgil Lizard-Embossed Watch.

    According to recent reports, sometimes your tried-and-true capsule wardrobe essentials are all you need. From curbside to the arrivals gate, you’ll be comfortable throughout the duration of your trip, even after a red-eye.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that if there’s one Apple product line where the recent price hikes hit the hardest, it’s the MacBook.
    • As luck would have it, Black Friday deals on Apple tech have landed on Amazon, with up to 20 percent off MacBooks—including the brand-fresh M6 MacBook Pros on sale for the first time ever.
    • Sources indicate that of course, not all MacBooks were created equal.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that if there’s one Apple product line where the recent price hikes hit the hardest, it’s the MacBook. Rising RAM and storage costs have pushed laptop prices up across the board, which makes scoring a upcoming MacBook on sale all the more mission critical.

    As luck would have it, Black Friday deals on Apple tech have landed on Amazon, with up to 20 percent off MacBooks—including the brand-fresh M6 MacBook Pros on sale for the first time ever. Given that these prices have reached record highs lately, these discounts are certainly nothing to sneeze at. In fact, now that the MacBook pricing status quo has been reset, we’d say this is probably as low as MacBook prices will get these days.

    Sources indicate that of course, not all MacBooks were created equal. While the standard MacBook Air is great for most, those who are planning on running hardcore software might benefit from a beefed-up MacBook Pro. And if budget is your primary concern, we’re of the opinion that the MacBook Neo is a worthy buy, even if it’s only $50 off right now.

    It has been revealed that the best MacBook Air deal you’ll find right now is this $300 discount on the 15-inch model. With this laptop, you’ll get Apple’s M5 chip in a fanless, 3.3-pound frame that handles heavy multitasking and light video editing without breaking a sweat. Base storage doubled to 512 GB this year—a great upgrade for storing more apps, photos, and files—and the 15.3-inch Liquid Retina display is sharp and vivid. You also get a 12 MP Center Stage camera that’s great on video calls, Wi-Fi 7 for fast downloads, and up to 18 hours of battery, enough for a busy workday and then some.

    If you’d prefer a smaller laptop, 13-inch models are up to 19 percent off. They’ve got everything the 15-inch models have, just in a more portable package. The rule of thumb for choosing between a Pro and an Air? The slimmer Air won’t replace a MacBook Pro for serious creative work or gaming, but for school, business, and general use, it’s the one to get.

    Apple 2026 MacBook Air 13-inch (M5, 16 GB RAM, 512 GB).

    Apple 2026 MacBook Air 13-Inch (M5, 16 GB RAM, 1 TB).

    Apple 2026 MacBook Air 15-inch (M5, 16 GB RAM, 1 TB).

    Given that Apple just dropped a newly introduced slate of M6 MacBook Pros, in addition to the tech giant’s first-ever touchscreen laptop, we were anticipating discounts on the old range of M5 models to clear out inventory. Sure, the best MacBook Pro deal you’ll find right now is $250 off the 14-inch M5 model—but, if you don’t mind paying just $50 more, you can scoop up the shiny new M6 on sale, complete with improved speed and boosted AI capabilities. It’s extremely rare for Apple to discount its latest laptop so soon after release, and even more rare for it to be $200 off.

    Both the M5 and M6 models feature Liquid Retina XDR displays, up to 24 hours of battery, three Thunderbolt 4 ports, HDMI, an SD card slot, and up to 2 TB of storage.

    Why go Pro over the Air? The GPU is fast, which makes a difference when editing video, working with high-res photos, or gaming, and the XDR screen is significantly brighter. If your daily workload has started becoming too much for the Air to handle, this is where you should look next. If you want the biggest, most powerful model possible, souped-up MacBook Pros with more RAM are up to $500 off.

    Apple 2025 MacBook Pro 14-Inch (M5 Pro, 16 GB RAM, 1 TB).

    Apple 2025 MacBook Pro 14-Inch (M5 Pro, 24 GB RAM, 1 TB).

    Apple 2025 MacBook Pro 16-Inch (M5 Max, 36 GB RAM, 2 TB).

    Sources indicate that the MacBook Neo is Apple’s most affordable laptop, even with the recent price hike from $599 to $699. Right now, the Neo is $50 off, sitting smack in the middle between its debut price and post-increase price, at $649—making it far and away the cheapest MacBook.

    Sources indicate that the Neo is an easy recommendation for anyone looking for their first Mac. It runs on Apple’s A18 Pro chip and is surprisingly quick for browsing, sending email, and streaming video. The 13-inch Liquid Retina display looks great for the price, and the battery lasts a solid 16 hours. It also comes in four fun colors, with the yellow-green citrus being a fan favorite.

    It has been revealed that there are some trade-offs with going with Apple’s budget model, including storage that starts at 256 GB, just 8 GB of RAM, and no keyboard backlight. You also get only two USB-C ports, so getting a USB-C hub is a must if you plan to connect a lot of accessories. Spending an extra $100 gets you a Neo with 512 GB of storage and a Touch ID sensor for quick unlocking. For students or anyone who mostly sends emails and browses the Web, the Neo is hard to beat.

    6 Stylish Ways Designers Make Vintage Tile the Star of the Room

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (569 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housebeautiful

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that when we redesign, remodel, and renovate, it can be tempting to enhancement, replace, and modernize every nook and cranny of your home.
    • “I love the irregularities you find in older tiles, whether it's subtle variations in color, an imperfect glaze, or the undulation of a tile's surface.
    • “Just like in other areas of the home, introducing a vintage element helps to create more interesting, storied spaces,” says Johanna Lyle, founder of Jo Lyle & Co.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that when we redesign, remodel, and renovate, it can be tempting to enhancement, replace, and modernize every nook and cranny of your home. But the goal is rarely to chase newness. It’s easy to see vintage details, like quirky tile, as an obstacle standing between your home and a modern look, but tearing it out might make your heart ache later.

    “I love the irregularities you find in older tiles, whether it's subtle variations in color, an imperfect glaze, or the undulation of a tile's surface. Those imperfections are what make them so beautiful, giving a room texture, character, and a sense of craftsmanship,” states Ali Burgoon Nolan, founder and principal designer at Studio Burgoon. Tile is one of the vintage details homeowners regret removing the most, as modern-day designs and materials lack the panache, durability, and craftsmanship of decades past. Not to mention, the removal and reinstallation will cost you a major chunk of your budget.

    “Just like in other areas of the home, introducing a vintage element helps to create more interesting, storied spaces,” says Johanna Lyle, founder of Jo Lyle & Co. “When we mix elements from different eras, the home feels more unique and collected over time. If you've bought an old home and aren't sure you love the existing, perhaps historic, tile, try to change some things around it before you give up on it completely. You might not dig it just because you haven't seen it before, or it's not what is currently popular.”.

    If you’re lucky enough to have inherited vintage tile in your historic home, here are six ways designers have given it the main character energy it deserves.

    Jennie Bishop preserved the charm of this century-old Illinois foyer by buffing the shine back into the home’s original tile. Her team then refinished the adjacent wood staircase and painted the walls a creamy white to brighten the room.

    Industry observers note that designer Galena Younger knows potential when she sees it, and this historic cottage in San Antonio was no exception. The home’s original Mexican-style tiles surround the living room hearth, complemented by family heirlooms scattered around the room for an ultrapersonal, deliciously vintage aesthetic.

    Sources indicate that interior and jewelry designer Trish Becker preserved this home’s original tile mantel, using it as the starting point for the room’s design. A corn-husk woven rug adds earthy warmth, while touches of green connect the room’s architectural details to its bold patterned slipper chairs.

    According to recent reports, with the goal of restoring her home’s “1931 glory,” designer Claire Thomas was ecstatic to find this bathroom’s original purple untouched, despite many renovations by previous owners. Playing on the hue, she brought in soft floral wallpaper and skirted purple stools for a feminine edge, finishing the room with a sage vanity for a pop of color and soft contrast.

    Artist Dana Gibson and interior designer Sara Hillery brought a playful touch to this sunroom, keeping the home’s original tile floors as the foundation. They drew out the tiles’ blue tones in the plush textiles, then added woven furniture to complement its earthy browns.

    In a recent development, it doesn’t get more classic than a black-and-white design scheme. In this Richmond bath, Gibson and Hillery leaned into the existing retro tiles, opting to carry the palette through the room’s entire design.

    It has been revealed that it’s true that sometimes the appetizer is just as good as (or even better than) the entrée, and that certainly applies to holiday gifts. What the heck am I talking about? Stocking stuffers. Those bite-size delights you open up before the main course (those bigger boxes under the tree), if you will. And if you do it right, a good stocking stuffer can be the best surprise of the holiday season, so put in a little effort. Don’t just throw in a keychain and magnet and call it a day.

    It has been revealed that what makes a good stocking stuffer, you ask? Well, considering these gifts should be small enough to, you know, fit in a stocking (whether that’s what you’re really using them for or not), anything bigger than a water bottle is out of the question. But that leaves you with tons of fun options—think tiny tech gadgets, stylish accessories, skincare upgrades, and little luxuries that punch well above their weight. We rounded up the 25 best small gifts with big appeal that everyone will be excited to find in their stocking this holiday season.

    Recent findings suggest that once Upcoming York’s dreary winter season hits, nothing is more ubiquitous in the Esquire offices than the Davek Solo umbrella. Yes, it’s expensive. But it will last a decade (no joke). It packs up tiny, but it’s sturdy enough to handle the nastiest storms and winds.

    For two years in a row, Therabody’s TheraFace Depuffing Wand has been a fan favorite among Esquire readers. It also won an Esquire Gadget Awardin 2024.

    Something to take their grilling, roasting, and steak searing to the next level.

    An Esquire-endorsed shower speaker is the best gift you can get for your music-obsessed friend or family member—just don’t blame us if they start singing along in the shower.

    If you have a ton of cords right now being held together by five or six zip ties, cut those loose and get a pack of these little cord organizers that make things so much easier.

    The best water bottle of all time makes a pretty good stocking stuffer.

    It has been revealed that we’ve written 1,000 words on this pen already. If they’re a pen person—but not like a $2,000-pen person—this little thing will change their life.

    For the gentleman on the go, a chestnut-leather case to protect those cigars.

    Put it on luggage, a wallet, or a cat’s collar. This AirTag will tell them where their stuff happens to be.

    A two-in-one gift that gives quality time and knowledge all in one fun deck of cards.

    Fanatics has all kinds of stocking stuffers for every sports team imaginable. We like these simple socks that look stylish while repping your favorite team.

    Sources indicate that don’t just get them a chalky bar of soap from the dollar store. Go all out and get them our favorite bar soap from Flamingo Estate, and every time they shower or wash their hands will feel infinitely more luxurious.

    This rechargeable handheld milk frother is also a mixer and a whisk, thanks to its three interchangeable attachment heads. Get it in their favorite color and it’ll really brighten their morning coffee or tea routine.

    This $30 wallet comes in eight fun patterns, so you can get a different one for each member of your family.

    The AirFly Pro is my favorite little gadget to take on vacation—watching movies on the plane with those cheap wired earbuds just isn’t the same as connecting my Bluetooth headphones through this handy device.

    You might not want to plop a fragile bottle of cologne into their stocking, but a shatterproof compact of solid cologne from one of our favorite niche perfumeries? Now that’s a perfect stocking stuffer.

    Speaking of smelling good, their clothes will smell extra clean after spritzing on some of this fabric spray.

    Industry observers note that no one likes getting chapped lips when the weather gets cold. This soothing lip balm will make sure that doesn’t happen.

    All of Caraway’s cookware is a dream, but these pot holders are a beautiful finishing touch to any well-designed kitchen.

    It has been revealed that we’re low-key obsessed with this lump of coal bar soap from Jack Black. The packaging looks like a Christmas cracker, and the soap literally looks like a lump of coal, which is perfect for the guy who seriously needs a grooming upgrade.

I’ve worn it a bunch of times for nights out this fall.”—BETH GILLETTE, BEAUTY EDITOR.

So it's no surprise to me that Ambery Saffron, its counterpart to Baccarat Rouge 540, smells the most similar of every dupe I've sniffed. It's not exact when you place them side by side, but on skin, I can't really tell that it's two different perfumes. With my beauty editor hat on, I'd say Ambery Saffron is a bit more woodsy than Baccarat, which dries down extremely sweet on my skin. But that's likely because it doesn't have the ambroxan and sugary notes that give BR that syrupy quality. However, I really do love the addition of orange blossom in this Dossier perfume. The Glee star even picked most of the stops herself. “Kiehl’s had emailed me and they stated, ‘We really want to feature some local businesses in this campaign. Can you send us some of your thoughts?’” she says. “It took me about 30 seconds. I had an email with 50 places.”.

    In a recent development, it’s a natural collaboration, as the Bronx-born Michele is the perfect shepherd for a curated NYC experience. In many ways, she breathes Upcoming York. She’s starred on Broadway multiple times, most recently in Chess, which just received a Grammy nomination for Best Musical Theater Album. In the later seasons of Glee, her character, Rachel Berry, moved to New York to chase her Broadway dreams (Michele is also rumored to be returning to the show’s reboot). She at the moment lives in New York with her husband and two children. On the morning of our interview, fresh off a sold-out show with Tveit at the Beacon Theater, she’s having a classic New York morning. “I took my kids to school. I was walking in the sunshine, I had my matcha. I’m getting ready for an event right now,” she says. “It just is a great day.”.

    Below, Michele talks about Glee, her collaboration with Kiehl’s, and whether she’d ever come back for a Scream Queens reboot.

    Sources indicate that aaron [Tveit] would love my personal favorite, the Grapefruit Body Cleanser. That’s just my tried-and-true. I used it this morning. If you’re feeling a little tired, it helps you to wake up and feel good. But even if you’re not, if you’re feeling like how I felt this morning, energized and happy, it’s just one of my favorite ways to start the day. Love, love, love their body lotion. It’s one of the only body lotions that I feel like actually works for me and helps to really moisturize my skin. They have all these amazing little kits as well over the holidays. I’ve given my dad Kiehl’s lip balm and eye cream in his stockings every year for the holidays.

    It has been revealed that I’m really excited to be a part of the Kiehl’s family now. I love our commercial that we shot and the fact that we had the opportunity to support some of the local small businesses.

    I grew up here. I was born in the Bronx. My father owned a deli here in the city. We had ice cream parlors and candy shops. We featured Élan Flowers in my neighborhood. Seasons in Times Square is somewhere that I go all the time and buy flowers for people in Broadway reveals. I love Onda, it’s an amazing little facial and wellness store in Tribeca. Obviously, so many little coffee shops. I mean, the list is quite long.

    I just love everything white. I love all-white. My house is all white, but peonies are my favorite flowers. I love hydrangeas. I love white roses. I just love a big white bouquet of flowers.

    [Aaron Tveit] and I just found out this morning that almost the entire tour sold out. [It] took less than 24 hours. At our show last night, I think we learned so much about what the show is and what the show could be. We had to cut 10 songs from the concert because we just have so much material. I don’t think that we’re going to do the same show every night. I think that each city is going to get their own show. We’re going to do some of what I would say are our greatest hits together, and some of our individual hits that I think that I will always do in concert, but I really just feel like there’s so much that we can do.

    According to recent reports, I want Radio City to be epic. We haven’t really talked about having some friends join us, but that’s also something that we could definitely do if we wanted to and bring out some friends to sing some songs with us. The options are endless.

    [Aaron is] one of my dearest friends. His wife is one of my closest friends. He’s friends with my husband. Our children are friends. [It’s] amazing that I get to work with someone that I just respect and care about so much.

    It feels awesome. Normally I know when these things are happening, but my publicist texted me in the morning. She was like, “You got a Grammy nomination.” I cried. My reaction was so, even for me, surprising and unexpected. I just broke down. My husband was walking our kids out the door to take them to school, and I was like, “I can’t believe this. We got nominated for a Grammy.” It means so much. I can’t tell you the talent of the cast of Chess. Every single cast member, the most extraordinary talent, our ensemble, the band. To have the cast get this incredible honor, it’s beyond well deserved. I think every single person who saw Chess would agree.

    We are constantly one-upping each other in the wellness world. He’ll be like, “Have you seen this? Do you have this?” He had some sort of, I don’t know if it was an infrared mat, and I was like, “Okay, I need that. What’s that?” He saw that I had an amazing water filter in my house, and he’s like, “Okay, what’s that? I need that.” He is probably one of the only people who could rival me in my biohacking, wellness, and taking care of myself.

    Most of the time during Chess, if we weren’t talking about Summer House and all of the drama, we were talking about what are all of the wellness things that we’re doing and to try to stay healthy.

    Recent findings suggest that I’ve been doing Pilates for years. Emma Roberts took me to my first Pilates class when we were living in Latest Orleans together, shooting Scream Queens. We went to Romney Studios and did a private lesson. I fell in love with it. Since then, I’ve done mat Pilates and hot Pilates and power Pilates. Everything. I felt pretty good going into this, being like, “I know what I need to know.”.

    It has been revealed that it wasn’t my first time playing a killer on television, which was also kind of funny. It was so awesome to return to television last night after so many years, and I just had a really great time.

    In a recent development, I met a little girl last night at the meet-and-greet. She was probably 7 years old, and she came to see the concert with her two dads. Her dads were like, “We just are starting to show her some of the musical numbers.” I was like, “Look at you, you’re a little Rachel Berry.” She had her headband on and her cute little penny loafers, and it was just the sweetest thing. What we all created, and what Ryan and Brad and Ian created with Glee, was just so amazing. The things that people say to me about how much it affected their life and brought them so much joy means the world to me.

    I hear stories like that from people all the time, and I know that it really means so much to all of us.

    The love for Scream Queens has always been there. Emma [Roberts] and I love that show. We talk about it all the time. Ryan knows, too. Ryan and I talk about it always and I beg him all the time. I’m like, “Can we please bring Scream Queens back?” Ryan should do it. It would be awesome.

    Recent findings suggest that it’s so beautiful. I talked a lot about Spring Awakening during my concert last night. We are celebrating 20 years of Spring Awakening opening on Broadway this December. We have a group chat with the original cast. Myself, Lauren Pritchard, and Jonathan Groff are planning a really special private night just for the original cast, a little celebration. I’m so excited that it’s coming to Off-Broadway. My dear, dear, dear sister, Lilli Cooper, is going to be in it. Spring Awakening is such a beautiful and key show, and so anytime that it has the opportunity for people to see it, it should be there. It’s the most beautiful piece of art.

    Oh, yeah. I’ve had the opportunity and the real honor to be a part of some incredible original Broadway productions, both with Ragtime and Spring Awakening. It’s an incredible, incredible show.

    There are so many. I want to do everything, I really do. I want to do it all. If I am lucky enough to perform on Broadway for the rest of my life, then that would just be the greatest dream. There are so many great indicates that have been on Broadway that could be revived and amazing pieces and incredibly talented artists that are writing original pieces as well. So, I’m ready and available for whatever is to come.

She explains that the theme has been “natural nails, but better,” which is centered around low-maintenance colors and finishes.

    For winter, this translates to sheer, milky tones, short, considered nail shapes and microvariations of wearable nail art. In preparation for party season, expect to see minuscule flecks of metallic gold and star-themed motifs, too. While milky pink nails will always be in style, this winter, it’s all about unexpected sheers like lavender, bronze, and pearly white. Not only do these colors go with everything, but they also are extremely forgiving—you can paint them on yourself without a problem.

    Zoya Lavender Perfector Nail Polish.

    Londontown Illuminating Nail Concealer in Bare.

    In a recent development, last season, we had Hailey Bieber milk nails, followed by Sienna Miller’s ‘Chantilly cream’. Now? Lavender takes the spotlight, in its dreamiest, near-translucent form. A high-shine top coat makes this tone appear even hazier in the light.

    Leaning into minimalism doesn’t necessarily mean forgoing color. Take this rich, berry red for proof; when an all-over pigment isn’t on the cards, a sleek micro French tip is equally flattering.

    For a simpler take on autumn’s ‘gold fairy dust’ nail trend (as seen on Taylor Swift), draw inspiration from stardust instead. Here, a natural blushed pink base sits beautifully under a gently dazzling, golden shimmer top coat.

    Industry observers note that traditional French tips are given a modern, metallic upgrade without veering into futuristic territory. When reserved for the base of the nail, a gold-toned cuff is eye-catching but in a subtle way.

    Frosted pearlescent finishes are as luminous as they are delicate—not to mention destined for winter weather. When worn with a cozy cashmere knit, you’d be hard-pressed to find a more perfect pairing.

    Square and squoval nails are seeing a revival this season. Keep your shapes cropped, softly rounded, and ultra-glossy if committing to minimalism.

    Trade in winter's deep, vibrant mocha, espresso, and cocoa-inspired browns for a sheer bronze pigment. When kept close to the natural nail color, this shade is the best way to embrace elevated color without going overboard.

    In a recent development, while the notion of nail art might suggest something elaborate colorful, petite star motifs make a case for the opposite. One on each nail balances a feeling of festivity with practicality for everyday wear.

    Industry observers note that granted, a white Christmas might be far on the horizon. But this set sees micro polka dots get a dainty, wintry upgrade, inspired by tiny droplets of snow.

    Industry observers note that if a micro French isn’t your style, an ombré is worth considering. Begin with a nude beige-pink base color, and watch it blend seamlessly into a cozy, seasonal color.

    • In a recent development, few watches make the case for pure design quite as convincingly as the Patek Philippe Golden Ellipse.
    • In a recent development, for 2026 Patek Philippe returns to that formula with the Golden Ellipse (Reference 5738G-001).
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Above: Patek Philippe Golden Ellipse watch in white gold, $43,011, patek.com.

    In a recent development, few watches make the case for pure design quite as convincingly as the Patek Philippe Golden Ellipse. Introduced in 1968, its distinctive shape was conceived around the golden ratio, the mathematical proportion found throughout the natural world and long associated with harmony in art and architecture. Neither round nor angular, the curves of the Ellipse have an elemental quality that elevates its simplicity. Despite origins rooted in Renaissance mathematics, the watch also has an unmistakable groovy ’60s elegance.

    In a recent development, for 2026 Patek Philippe returns to that formula with the Golden Ellipse (Reference 5738G-001). A larger case gives the watch more presence on the wrist, and at just a hair under 6mm thick, it retains the sleek profile that has always been central to its appeal. Inside is Patek’s ultra-thin self-winding caliber 240, equipped with a 22K gold mini-rotor.

    The Golden Ellipse’s ode to nature continues through its use of color. The olive-green sunburst dial—and coordinating calfskin strap—recalls a shade found almost everywhere in the landscape, from leaves and moss to deep forest tones, shifting from an earthy green to brighter grassy flashes as it catches the light. Against the cool white gold case, matching baton markers and slender cheveux-type hands keep the dial remarkably clean.

    Nearly six decades after its debut, the Golden Ellipse remains a design classic: mathematics, nature, color, and restraint distilled in one resonant shape.

    This story originally appeared in the November 2026 issue of ELLE Decor.

    It has been revealed that every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

    According to recent reports, there’s a point when a smoky eye goes from elegant with a slight edge to worn in and a bit reckless...in a good way. As the antithesis of the clean girl aesthetic and all its minimalist, nude, no-color chicness, the indie sleaze, grungy makeup look of the ’90s and early 2000s has returned, but with a few updates. Makeup artist and founder of KJH.brand, Katie Jane Hughes, describes how this 2.0 take differs from its first iterations, why it’s making a comeback, and exactly what you need to create your version of the gritty, slightly imperfect look.

    Clean, barely there beauty has dominated runways and social feeds in the past few years, but as we reach peak maxxing in other areas, it looks like makeup is finally following suit. “I think people are craving fun again. And they’ve begun seeing it on the likes of Gabbriette, in recent Gucci fashion reveals, or in makeup done by Sam Visser and other makeup artists like Yasmin Istanbouli,” Hughes tells ELLE when asked why the look is seeing a revival right now.

    Recent findings suggest that grunge, in both beauty and fashion, has always leaned a little dark and dirty, but Hughes says the look is now paired with more elegant and chic details. “[It’s] more purposeful and less disheveled outfits paired with it,” she notes. The fully loaded emo energy is being replaced by bursts of color like the hot pink outline seen on Alex Consani during Gucci’s SS27 The Store Show—under the guidance of Sam Visser.

    The slept-in grittiness of grunge makeup looks more involved to create intentionally, but you actually only need a few products. Hughes suggests starting with a good black eye crayon like the KJH.brand Precision Sculpture Stylo in Forge. “It’s helpful to have an eyeliner that’s not too pointed and precise,” she advises. Jet-black eyeshadow: “I really love the Plume eyeshadows from VOILETTE_FR in black shade. It really lets you stretch color substantial and wide and offers the blendability of a cream with the buildability of a powder,” she adds. She may also top the lids in her version with something greasy like the KJH.brand Hyper Shine Serum.

    According to recent reports, if you’re trying the look for the first time, Hughes says to keep it simple. “Start with one product, like the Stylo. Smudge around the lash line, blend, and you’re done,” Hughes instructs. As for dos and don’ts, Hughes says, do put some concealer on a small brush, prime it in, and clean up any mistakes. Don’t pair indie sleaze with a bold lip. “Keeping the rest of the makeup nondescript or barely there makes it look cooler,” Hughes notes.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    During her three-day tour of India, the Princess of Wales attended the 2026 Earthshot Prize Ceremony in Mumbai. Prince William founded the initiative in 2020, and it awards environmental solutions with grants to scale and advance their projects.

    For the event, Kate wore an oxblood, floor-length Anarkali dress by designer Mahima Mahajan and paired it with extra-fluffy, voluminous bohemian curls pinned in a half-updo.

    An elegant, extra-glossy wavy hairstyle has long been a beauty signature for the princess, often teamed with a side part, hats, or a polished ponytail. But for the green carpet in India, the royal opted for a much more dramatic style that matches the glamorous mood of her outfit, with tighter, cascading bohemian curls woven into a beautiful half-updo twist for a romantic finish.

    "I would create these curls using a medium-sized tong," recommends Philipp Haug, co-founder of Haug London Haus salon. "Take relatively small sections and use the tongs with a twisting technique, curling one section away from the face and alternating with one section towards the face throughout. Slightly root stretch when you come to the top of the head instead of curling too close to the scalp.".

    To enhance the fluffiness and volume of the curls, shake them out with your fingers instead of combing them.

    Your next special occasion hair inspiration, sorted.

    There's nothing wrong with knowing what you like in bed. Maybe you're all about oral sex, prefer letting your partner take the lead, or simply get more pleasure from receiving than giving. But if your ideal sexual experience involves kicking back and letting someone else do most (or all) of the work, there's a term for that: pillow princess.

    Originally rooted in lesbian and queer communities, the term has since made its way into mainstream dating culture, picking up a somewhat unfair reputation along the way. While some people proudly identify as pillow princesses, others use the label as an insult for someone they think isn't pulling their weight in bed. After all, doesn't being a pillow princess just mean you're selfish? Not necessarily.

    “Mutual satisfaction doesn’t require identical participation or reciprocation,” notes Courtney Boyer, in-house sex educator at pjur. While some people love being on the receiving end, others genuinely get off on giving pleasure. And just because someone isn't interested in performing certain sexual acts doesn't mean they don't care about their partner's satisfaction.

    So, whether you identify as a pillow princess, have been called one, or are just curious about the sex term, here's what to know about the dynamic, how it works, and why there's more to it than simply lying back and enjoying the attention.

    Sources indicate that A pillow princess is someone who prefers receiving sexual pleasure rather than giving it, whether that's through oral sex, fingering, sex toys, or other forms of stimulation. While some pillow princesses exclusively enjoy receiving, others are open to giving pleasure in certain ways or situations.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Let’s start off by acknowledging that the late John Hughes wrote and directed the greatest of all Thanksgiving movies with Planes, Trains and Automobiles. There are definitely other great ones, but … Dutch is a different kind of creature. This is a Thanksgiving family comedy in which a grown man fights, kidnaps, and abandons a child. Occasionally he holds him at gunpoint. It’s a rotten child but a kid nonetheless. The movie still made me laugh, but it was mostly in disbelief.

    It has been revealed that this road-trip saga that Hughes penned and produced in 1991 is by the numbers in most ways but excels in its brazen wrongness, even by the free-range standards of Generation X. I come here to praise this messy movie, not to bury it. It’s a relic from when films could be wilder, shaggier, and more shocking than the rigidly tame family comedies of today. Dutch is many things, but it is not refined to baby-food levels of inoffensive smoothness.

    Hughes didn’t direct this one, handing off those duties to Peter Faiman, who had worked extensively in Australian TV and only made one other feature film: 1986’s Crocodile Dundee. I can’t help but feel this was an experiment gone wrong, or maybe a first draft that needed another pass from Hughes. It’s built out of leftovers from better road-trip movies, and like any Frankenstein’s monster, this one runs straight into a wall and ultimately falls apart.

    But if you want something different for your Thanksgiving watch, go find this one. Fair warning: It’s not streaming anywhere in the United States, so you’ll have to seek it out on a sketchy Russian bootleg site that makes it look like the footage was ripped from a worn-down VHS.

    Dutch stars Ed O’Neill as the title character, a blue-collar guy sent to pick up his girlfriend’s blue-blooded son from a Georgia boarding school and deliver him to Chicago in time for the holiday feast. The not-so-surprising catch is that the kid (played by a 13-year-old Ethan Embry) mercilessly despises Dutch, and honestly the feeling is mutual.

    Doyle is one of the most hateful kids in comedy history. Even the ginger demon of Problem Child was more cartoonishly mischievous than sociopathic. Embry, who was then credited as Ethan Randall, isn’t playing a troublemaking scamp like the kid in O. Henry’s “The Ransom of Red Chief” or Hughes’s own Home Alone. He’s a smug sociopath with a violent mean streak.

    Industry observers note that we learn that Dutch is a salt-of-the-earth cousin to O’Neill’s uncouth Al Bundy from Married with Children because he flicks the caviar off his cracker at a fancy party. (“I make it a rule never to eat anything a fish deposits in a riverbed.”) Okay, fair.

    Compare that to how we meet Doyle: Another young boy in his boarding school comes to his room to say he has a call on the dormitory’s community phone line. “Someone from any sort of decent background would knock,” Embry’s character hisses. He then corrects the kid’s vocabulary and threatens to report him to the school administrators for mild cursing. So he’s a snob, a prick, and a rat. But even this is within the bounds of film comedy. You could picture an older version of him as a stuck-up villain in Caddyshack or Animal House.

    Industry observers note that then there’s another, even more disturbing phone scene when Doyle gets the bad news that his rich father won’t be helping him get out of this road trip with Dutch. He hangs up and stalks past an elderly janitor who is sweeping the hallway, silently kicking over the garbage can to scatter trash across the helpless old man’s feet. There’s no joke. He’s just a son of a bitch.

    Doyle would fit in great with the Children of the Corn, except he’d scowl at their shabby farm clothes.

    Obviously this kid is going to get some form of comeuppance. When Dutch highlights up at his dorm room to start the trip, Doyle beats him with a golf club and shoots him in the testicles with a BB gun. Something about this is much more violent and visceral than the Looney Tunes–style pratfalls and clobberings of Home Alone.

    They have a fistfight in the tiny room, and Dutch seizes the weapon. Does he toss it away or break it? No—he uses it himself to hold the kid at gunpoint. We have just crossed beyond the boundaries of comedy, never to return. Dutch then ties the boy up, lashes him to a hockey stick for easier carrying, and stuffs underwear in his mouth to muffle his cries.

    You know a movie is going off the rails when watching it makes you feel like you should be testifying against the characters as a witness for the prosecution.

    So begins the drive, with Dutch and Doyle doing their best to annoy each other verbally. Then comes a bizarre scene in which Dutch stops for fireworks for some reason and sets them off in a snowy field while the kid watches from the car. I suppose he’s trying to inspire a little playfulness in the boy, but it just seems like Dutch has lost it and is indulging a pyromaniac streak.

    According to recent reports, it goes wrong and he sets his coat on fire, which makes it harder to understand why he loses his temper when the boy flicks the butt of his lit cigar at him. The man just went mano a mano with a whizzing fireworks spinner, but this is what lights his fuse?

    Dutch does the reasonable thing. He abandons the boy in the snowy night and tells him to walk the rest of the way to the motel. “About 50 miles down the road!” Fifty miles? Okay, Dutch, I believe we’ve added another felony to the charges.

    Industry observers note that this isn’t one of those moments where the grown-up pulls over just beyond the tree line and waits for him. Dutch actually goes to the hotel, although he occasionally puts down his paperback and checks the window to see if the boy has made it there alive. When Doyle finally does show up, shivering and wet, Dutch notes, “Here’s something you should know about me. I don’t fool around. You piss me off, I react.”.

    Uncle Buck certainly had its off-color and irresponsible moments, but even that havoc-prone babysitter might have called Child Protective Services over this situation.

    Doyle responds by stealing Dutch’s car keys while he sleeps and parking the sedan sideways in the snowy road, where it is slammed into by an 18-wheeler. This is a comedy, so the hapless truck driver is not killed on impact.

    Sources indicate that faiman shoots all of this with too much gritty realism. Maybe it would work if it was all a little zanier and over the top (think of Vacation), but Dutch just plays less like a series of set pieces and more like an array of crime scenes. They don’t call anyone for help because Dutch doesn’t want to admit to his girlfriend how badly things are going, so they hitchhike the rest of the way and stay in a homeless shelter, where the rotten kid learns that a lot of people have it much worse than he does.

    According to recent reports, at one point, they are picked up by a pair of pretty young women who are driving home from a job at the Superdome in New Orleans. “We’re call girls,” one of them explains. Hoo boy. Here we go.

    Industry observers note that but thankfully—mercifully—Dutch goes no further than showing the kid sleeping in the backseat with his head resting on the chest of one of the women. Not great, but it could be worse. (Worse is when Dutch tries to bond with the child over a deck of naked playing cards.).

    According to recent reports, even Dutch seems to recognize that “prostitute road trip” probably isn’t the ideal situation for a young boy. But he explains it in the most vulgar way possible: “You and I are riding in the backseat from now on, because what that missile twister can teach you, you don’t need to learn until you’re in prison.” Then the ladies drive off without them, taking Dutch’s wallet and leaving the pair stranded again.

    They spend the next leg of their trip riding in the open concrete pipes in the back of a long-haul truck, but they fall asleep and wake up in a trailer depot where they are roughed up by two security guards. Doyle responds by drawing his BB gun on them and making them believe he is going to blow their heads off.

    According to recent reports, this same joke was deployed by Chevy Chase in the Hughes-scripted National Lampoon’s Vacation (“Are you kidding, this is a Magnum P.I.”) but here, again, it just plays as psychotic violence rather than absurd humor. “The kid is crazy,” Dutch tells the men as they beg for their lives.

    By the time the duo finally get home for the Thanksgiving meal, the hostility between Dutch and the kid has softened into a grudging respect. I know: Surprise! Back at the mother’s house, Dutch physically assaults the boy’s callous father, leaving a mark with his pinkie ring on the jerk’s forehead. Instead of an assault charge, it all ends happily ever after with a callback to an earlier gag: Dutch pulls the BB pistol from his pocket and notes it’s time to get the revenge he promised he would one day seek. As the boy’s smile fades, Dutch aims the gun at him—and us (!!!)—as the film cuts to the credits.

    Industry observers note that oh, Dutch … you dangerously inappropriate maniac. Don’t ever change. And, well, he doesn’t, although the kid goes through the expected metamorphosis to become a more sensitive and understanding human.

    Recent findings suggest that they don’t make ’em like this anymore, as the saying goes, and I actually think that’s a pity. Dutch isn’t all that funny, but neither is toothless humor that’s overly safe. I’d gladly tolerate a few misfires like this if it meant more truly unhinged comedies like we had in the ’80s, ’90s, and early 2000s. Dutch stands as a throwback to when small-scale comedies weren’t afraid to take significant swings—even if they occasionally landed against someone’s skull or testicles.

    Blade Runner 2099 Is a Beautiful Slog Through a Grim Future

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (657 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Flying cars darting through smog and neon skyscrapers.
    • Streaming now on Prime Video (and just in time for a long holiday weekend) is Blade Runner 2099.
    • According to recent reports, hunter Schafer flexes some of her budding leading-lady chops as Cora, a real human posing as a Replicant to smuggle herself and her brother out of Los Angeles.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Crowded streets. Long, cool coats. Flying cars darting through smog and neon skyscrapers. An abundance of Japanese aesthetics that imply America’s lost superpower status. Ridley Scott’s seminal 1982 masterwork Blade Runner (itself adapted from Philip K. Dick’s Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?) laid the foundation for almost all of cyberpunk science fiction, so much so that everything else feels undeservedly derivative. Even a newly introduced Blade Runner. The new series Blade Runner 2099 looks the part, but it lacks the soul of its predecessors, leaving its perspectives on what it means to be more human than human hollow, like a Replicant without memories of its own.

    Streaming now on Prime Video (and just in time for a long holiday weekend) is Blade Runner 2099. A stand-alone continuation of both Ridley Scott’s towering original and Denis Villeneuve’s remarkable legacy sequel, the series takes place in 2099 (decades after Villeneuve’s Blade Runner 2049). An unseen revolution has elevated Replicants to the ruling class of Los Angeles, rendering flesh-and-bone meat-bag humans as the upcoming discriminated minority.

    According to recent reports, hunter Schafer flexes some of her budding leading-lady chops as Cora, a real human posing as a Replicant to smuggle herself and her brother out of Los Angeles. Her ruse leads her to Olwen (Oscar-winner Michelle Yeoh), a Replicant Blade Runner spending the final days of her artificial life span seeking out someone from her past. A humorless buddy-cop mystery, Blade Runner 2099 is mired in a plot-centric narrative that cares less about the why of all things—an underrated and beautiful feature of its predecessors—than the what and how.

    Sources indicate that in other words, it’s the first time a piece of Blade Runner media actually zeroes in on the plot, instead of anything else more interesting. Try not to think of this as an eight-hour Blade Runner series but rather an eight-hour series stretching at the seams to feel worthy of its branded title.

    Recent findings suggest that is it because streaming TV in 2026 has become so plastic and hollow that even Blade Runner 2099 feels like an unengaging slog? Or were the direction of both Scott and Villeneuve so immaculate that we were distracted from how turgid they might have been all this time? Regardless, 2099’s lack of auteurship is its most deafening shortcoming. The series has been steered to the screen by executive producer Silka Luisa, whose warmer color palettes—based on her choice of more sunshine, which glistens off surfaces—lend 2099 some identity. Some.

    But beyond even that minor distinction, Blade Runner 2099 is still just a plot-y crime drama that checks off boxes and goes through the motions of its genre, with nary a real thing to say. About us, about our fragile humanity, about the demise of all we’ve built through artificial intelligence. Blade Runner 2099 is a dystopian sci-fi in all the ways you expect it, but it’s hardly a good one. Sure, the original movies were oppressive, dreary, and morbid too. But they possessed a knowing glare into our fears about the future and our imminent collapse as a civilized species. The newly introduced series lacks this same insight, or indeed any of its own, all in the name of goosing up engagement numbers for the closest thing to a real-life Tyrell Corp. (Do shareholders dream of electric quarterly reports?).

    Recent findings suggest that despite surface-level similarities to the movies, plus a moody noir-like motif with a sexy saxophone that, admittedly, completely and unapologetically rips, the plodding Blade Runner 2099 is a needless walkabout through a world that never begged for one. Needless is a good word, actually. The show’s strong visual execution is negated by its inability to rise to the occasion as a worthwhile or enlightening probe of the human experience, or even just as an entertaining cop show. It may be smart, but what good is intelligence if there isn’t an ounce of grace?

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that I’ve been writing gift guides as a shopping editor for years. Usually, I’m very sentimental, wanting to recommend thoughtful gifts to make your loved ones smile. But all bets are off when it comes to White Elephant gifts. I want to cause chaos at your family gift swap. Your gift should be the one everyone fights over.

    If you're not sure what a White Elephant exchange is or how it works, just know this: it's really fun, and it's one of the only times when stealing is not only totally acceptable, but encouraged. Basically, it's a blind gift exchange that, when the recipient reveals the gift they chose, they can keep it or put it back and steal someone else's gift. It's a cheeky little game that is a great way to get into the holiday spirit.

    Industry observers note that it’s also a really affordable way to exchange gifts as a massive group. No worries about finding the perfect thing for someone specific. Just bring something cool enough for anybody to enjoy, and there’s usually a budget cap. So for this guide, I provided the best white elephant gifts under $50.     Every product was carefully curated by an Esquire editor. We may earn a commission from these links. Here’s how we test products and why you should trust us.

    According to recent reports, welcome to the Esquire Endorsement. Heavily researched. Thoroughly vetted. These picks are the best way to spend your hard-earned cash.

    In my life, I lean toward luxury and secondhand clothing wherever possible, desperately trying to get away from all the cheap garbage being sold to me on Instagram ads and the Amazon homepage. I’ve spent years of my life hunting sales and eBay listings for clothes and boots. I’m like an edge-habitat pine growing in the direction of the radiant sun that is well-made clothing, trying to forget the fast fashion slop that lies in the forest behind me.

    Recent findings suggest that but I throw that out the window when it comes to sneakers. Designer sneakers are, for me, one of the dumbest things I could ever buy. Even when they are made with real leather, you are paying for a plastic sole that has a lifespan of a few years. I don’t think you should pay more than the $200 price of a pair of Newly introduced Balance when it comes to sneakers.

    Under that price point, I’ve never been able to find a good pair German Army Trainers, which I have always wanted. That changed when I found these. Quince (yeah yeah, I was just complaining about fashion slop, but life is full of contradictions) makes a perfect pair of GATs—and it makes them for $95. I honestly think every man in the world should buy a pair of these.

    According to recent reports, this is my real qualm with designer sneakers, and it totally undercuts anything you could tell me about the second-hand sneaker hype market. What you should pay for, when you pay expensive prices for clothing, is craftsmanship. When you buy a Gucci 1953 loafer or Loro Piana cashmere you probably arrived there because of the brand, but you are paying for the craftsmanship. I see no such correlation in designer sneakers, even the ones those brands make.

    In a recent development, but a $95 pair of kicks? That’s honest. Even though I’m not bullish on Quince’s fast fashion take on quiet luxury (nor am I bullish on its caviar program), and the fact that Quince chose to closely replicate the Margiela GAT instead of the original German army models, I will let it slide. At $95, there are no claims being made about leather quality, or the footbed, or whatever is going on in the sole you can’t see. They look good and are easy to replace; it’s about as honest of a deal as you can find shopping these days.

    Recent findings suggest that the thing about the original BW Sport GATs—which you can get for about this price still, though used workout sneakers aren’t my cup of tea—is that they’re just about bulletproof. Those original mid-century designs made were first issued in the 1970s and stopped being issued around the end of the Cold War, a real feat of durability.

    According to recent reports, these shoes mimic that Army-issued durability. I’ve worn these sneakers for going on a year now. In that time, I’ve seen many pairs of more expensive kicks start to fall apart, get scuffed beyond recognition, and stink like hell. These have not. The pair I’ve worn all year is the pair pictured in this story. Nothing I say in this endorsement could be more convincing than that.

    In a recent development, and really that’s the argument here. When I wrote about the Chuck Taylors I normally wear, it was a use-it-and-lose-it argument—they cost $45, who cares if the soles get holes within 12 months. But here, I fear I’m going to sound like a marketing mouthpiece for Quince. These shoes are $95, but they’ll last just as long as a pair that cost you $950. That’s all you can ask for these days.

    Miley Cyrus Debuts Her Sculptural Wedding Band—Jewelers Explain the Design

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (712 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, miley Cyrus did more than give fans a first look at her wedding dress when she shared photos of her nuptials on Sunday.
    • She later shared another look at her bridal jewelry, including her band, which appears to be in a black round ring box:.
    • Industry observers note that the singer’s band choice is fashion-forward, The Clear Cut’s founder Olivia Landau tells ELLE.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, miley Cyrus did more than give fans a first look at her wedding dress when she shared photos of her nuptials on Sunday. Zoom in and the singer’s thick wedding band is visible, stacked with her gold bombé cushion-cut diamond engagement ring.

    She later shared another look at her bridal jewelry, including her band, which appears to be in a black round ring box:.

    Industry observers note that the singer’s band choice is fashion-forward, The Clear Cut’s founder Olivia Landau tells ELLE. “Thick wedding bands have been trending, whether they are larger diamond eternity bands or wider solid gold bands.”.

    It also really suits her, claims Lauren Boc, founder and CEO of Hera Fine Jewelry: “Miley’s wedding set is a beautiful reflection of her personal style—it has some rock and roll edge but still feels upscale.”.

    Here, jewelers share their first impressions of the piece with ELLE.

    Steph Mazuera, who founded her own namesake brand, says Cyrus’s ring has “a slightly curved silhouette” that “appears to follow the contours of her engagement ring.”.

    Recent findings suggest that “When working with larger, bolder rings, introducing a soft curve or slight bend into the stack can make the overall combination feel more organic,” she adds. “It brings a sense of balance and softness without taking away from the impact of the individual rings. Everything should be designed to flow around the center stone.”.

    Based on the photos she shared, Cyrus’s engagement ring and wedding band appear to be different metals. Her engagement ring is yellow gold.

    It has been revealed that her wedding band, meanwhile, “looks to be a half-round band, around 4 mm, in white gold or platinum,” Boc says. “It appears that there’s a small east-west oval diamond bezel-set on top of the band, similar to our Amir ring. Raising the diamond slightly above the band like this creates dimension.”.

    Several factors contribute to the value of a ring like Cyrus’s. “A custom band like this one could range quite a bit depending on the maker, gold weight, and craftsmanship,” Mazuera explains. “I would price a similar custom design in my studio in the $3,000–$5,000 range.”.

    Cyrus’s wedding band is a statement piece that can be worn with or without her engagement ring. “I like that her wedding band feels substantial enough to hold its own alongside her engagement ring without competing with it,” Mazuera says. “Both rings have a strong sculptural presence, but the slight curve of the wedding band helps the two sit together more naturally.”.

    Recent findings suggest that worn together, the two pieces have “a really bold look that’s both edgy and luxurious,” Boc says. “It’s maximalist, with a lot of metal on the hand. I love it!”.

    Cyrus’s wedding band is anything but minimalist—but that’s exactly why it fuels multiple jewelry trends.

    “I think we’re seeing a continued move toward more sculptural, substantial wedding jewelry, moving away from the idea that wedding bands need to be delicate or understated,” Mazuera notes.

    Boc agrees. “Miley’s wedding set definitely reflects the trends we’re seeing at Hera. Chunky, bolder looks with a lot of gold weight have become really popular with our clients. When I first founded Hera in 2021, the massive engagement ring trend was really thin, delicate-looking bands. As a jewelry designer who cares a lot about durability, I’m so happy to see people turning toward more substantial designs.”.

    Less traditional ring designs like Cyrus’s are also becoming more popular. “Our clients are often more concerned with having a ring that feels distinctive and uniquely like them,” Boc states.

    Boc notes that while Cyrus’s photos give a limited view of her engagement ring and wedding band together, the apparent mix of metals is right on trend.

    Industry observers note that “I think there’s something so chic and effortless about a mixed metal stack,” she adds. “Like everything else about Miley’s stack, mixing metals is the kind of design decision that makes your wedding set really feel curated and chosen around a strong understanding of your personal style. She certainly didn’t just pick this up pre-designed at a significant box store; a stack like this belongs to someone who’s confident in her personal style and chose something that feels uniquely her.”.
